Why Trust your Apple Shipments to MSC?

Experts in Reefer Container Transport

MSC operates a world-class reefer fleet, incorporating the very latest technology. Apples from New Zealand often travel some of the longest reefer sea miles to access European markets, and MSC’s advanced reefer technology help ensure the apples reach their destination as fresh as the day they left the shores of the North or South island.

MSC’s PRIMELINE and NaturaLINE containers are the most efficient and environmentally friendly refrigeration units available, keeping perishable fruit like apples in optimum conditions throughout their time with us.

How are Apples Shipped?

Like any fruit, great care needs to be taken of apples during their transport, especially from New Zealand where sea journeys of 10,000 miles or more may be required. After harvesting the apples should be stored in temperatures between 0°C to +4°C.

During shipping the cooling process continues. The temperature of reefer containers that contain apples should not fall below freezing. If they do there is a risk of apples spoiling. Equally, if exposed to warmer temperatures apples will sweat and moisten, with a risk of bacterial infection. Humidity in containers should be maintained at 90-95%.

Service Beyond the Port

MSC’s intermodal solutions provide safe and integrated transportation throughout the entire apple cargo supply chain, saving time and simplifying operations, integrating logistics from farm to port. Offering truck and rail solutions before and after ocean transport, MSC provides tailor-made solutions to care for your apple cargo.

Did you know?

New Zealand exports apples to around 80 countries in total.

Why Trust your Avocado Exports to MSC?

Delivering a Superfood

Dubbed a superfood for its nutrition and health qualities, consumers all over the world can't get enough of the avocado. To preserve the product's relatively short shelf-life requires a shipping partner with a high level of specialist knowledge and the right technology.

MSC assists avocado producers from countries, including Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Israel, to safely transport their precious cargo to retailers in Europe, Asia and the US – facilitating market access and extending shelf life.

Kept in Perfect Condition

With one of the world’s largest, greenest and most advanced reefer container fleets, we understand the importance of preserving refrigerated cargo from the moment we receive it until it reaches the end customer.

Our proven experience in transporting perishable goods is built on consistent investment in technology and infrastructure. This includes the use of CA units to slow down the ripening process and extend the shelf-life of avocados, enabling them to be transported for long distances without damaging their appearance, flavour or quality.

Learn more

Door-to-door Support

MSC offers tailor-made transport solutions across road, rail and sea, as well as pre-trip inspections where available, to ensure the best door-to-door service and equipment to meet your requirements. We provide our customers with door-to-door support and expert advice on everything from cargo-stuffing to customs paperwork.

We work closely with local growers, farmers and producers to understand their specific needs.

Helping Everyone to Enjoy Delicious, Fresh Produce, all Year Round

Looking for inland transportation, additional storage or administrative support? We’ve got you covered.

Why Trust your Banana Shipments to MSC?

Tailored to your Supply Chain

Our shipping routes cover the world’s top banana-producing regions, including Ecuador, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Nicaragua, China and the Philippines. Thanks to our flexible approach, we adapt our capacity (plugs and equipment) to meet the dynamics of the bananas peak season.

Cutting-edge Reefer Technology

To keep your fruit in the best possible condition, our world-leading reefer fleet features the latest temperature control technology, as well as vent settings to optimize air circulation. Our integrated Controlled Atmosphere (CA) helps slow down the ripening by removing ethylene and regulating O2 and CO2 to keep bananas green and fresher for longer.

Friendly, Professional Support

Our worldwide team of more than 1,000 reefer experts is available to support you throughout the shipping process. With more than five decades of experience in transporting fruit, we specialize in creating tailor-made door-to-door solutions to meet each customer's needs.

Go Further

Bananas are extremely sensitive to changes in temperature or humidity, as well as transit times: if conditions are too warm, they will ripen too quickly, while cold temperatures can cause dark chilling spots and other damage.

Looking for inland transportation or support with customs paperwork? We’ve got you covered.

Count on us for your Cherry Exports

Cherries are one of the world’s most popular fruits, a sweet ingredient of jams, cakes and confectionery, as well as being tasty treats themselves. Türkiye and the US are two of the biggest cherry producing nations.

Cherries are often consumed in their country of origin because of their short storage life and sensitive texture. Transporting cherries overseas requires specialist equipment to keep the produce feeling fresh, tasting sweet and looking good.

MSC has a wealth of experience in shipping cherries, from local experts in the supply chain to our reefer specialists, ensuring that this sweet cargo reaches its final destination in perfect condition.

Why Ship your Cherries with MSC

Cutting-edge Reefer Technology

Consumers today expect a constant supply of fresh, tasty and visually appealing fruit. Our world-class reefer fleet is equipped with the temperature control & dehumidification technology you need to preserve the taste, freshness, texture and aroma of cherries.

Additionally, we use Cold Treatment as a chemical-free way to eliminate fruit flies and other insects that might damage the biodiversity and agricultural industries of importing countries.

Also integrated within our containers are Controlled Atmosphere (CA) technologies, as well as other atmosphere control technologies such as

StarCool® CA

XtendFRESH®

Liventus®

Maxtend®

Purfresh®

Cooling and Storage

Cherries are stone fruits, so are very sensitive to despoiling after being harvested. The way they are handled and stored during the shipping process is critical. Sweet cherries should be cooled to temperatures below 5°C no more than four hours after harvest.

During transportation this chilling process must be continued. The temperature of containers that contain cherries should be kept at between 1.1 – 2.2°C, with a relative humidity of 90-95%. Cherries also require specific ventilation conditions. Containers should have an airflow of 60-80 circulations per hour with a continuous supply of fresh air.

If you have any questions about the services we offer for shipping cherries, please do not hesitate to get in touch.

Door-to-door Solutions

MSC offers tailor-made transport solutions across road, river, and sea to ensure the very best door-to-door service to meet your requirements. Our modern, efficient fleet, combined with our fast and reliable connections, helps improve producers’ access to markets and take quality fruits worldwide.

The ‘cherry on top of the cake’? MSC is one of the most reliable carriers in the world, with outstanding global schedule reliability.

Leverage on our extensive shipping network, connecting all major markets and even the most remote destinations. With our worldwide coverage you can ensure your produce will reach customers wherever they are.

Enjoy a seamless shipping experience with reliable transit times and a full portfolio of solutions at your service.

Intermodal Solutions to Fit your Needs

Enjoy a seamless transportation experience through a combination of sea, rail, and road solutions, crafted by experts and tailored to your needs. With our intermodal capabilities and expertise, you can trust us to get your citrus to market on time.

Save time and simplify your operations with top-level logistics solutions from farms to the port.

Experts in Reefer Transportation

Reefer containers need to meet specific requirements in order to keep cargo safe and comply with the required Cold Treatment protocols. Our fleet uses the Star Cool system, which maintains temperature in a simple and effective way, saving more energy. In the last few years, MSC added more than 5,000 units of this container type to our fleet ensuring greater coverage and a better service.

Count on us for your Seasonal Mango Shipments

Mangoes are fragile, perishable goods that must be picked, handled and transported with the highest level of care. With an annual harvest time that can be as short as six weeks, farmers and exporters require a flexible shipping partner that can scale up rapidly during peak mango season and provide the necessary containers and equipment to keep the fragile fruit cool and safe throughout its journey.

Shipping mangoes requires the highest level of care and specific temperature control to preserve their taste, aromatic and colouring characteristics. At MSC, we follow highly standardized control procedures to guarantee optimal transport conditions from pick-up to delivery.

Reefer container (20’, 40’ High Cube) availability

Controlled atmosphere

Dehumidification systems for optimal fruit preservation

More than 43 million tonnes of mangoes are produced globally every year.

Why Trust your Mango Exports to MSC?

A Specialist in Shipping
Perishable Cargo

Since mangoes will continue to ripen after harvest, it is essential to carefully control conditions throughout their transport. Using our Controlled Atmosphere technology, we slow down the ripening process and preserve the quality of your mangoes during transportation. Combined with MSC iReefer for the live monitoring of gas emissions, we give you greater control and peace of mind, ensuring your mangoes arrive at their destination in optimal condition.

A Safe Pair of Hands

Retailers expect the fruit to arrive in perfect condition, with consistent colour, shape, taste and aroma, and free from fruit flies. We employ high-quality reefer services and equipment to keep your fruit in perfect condition during transport, from packing plant to warehouse and supermarket shelf.

Learn more

Tailor-made Solutions

Our customer support team is always on hand to help, including assisting with documentation and regulatory compliance, while our cutting-edge technology enables easy tracking and monitoring of the fruit throughout its journey.

Learn more

Because you Need more than
Port-to-Port Services

Looking for extra storage, inland transportation or support with customs paperwork? We’ve got you covered.

From the African continent to Mexico, India and Thailand, we provide a tailor-made combination of inland transportation and shipping services for mango exporters around the world.

Overview

FAQs

Why Ship Vegetables with MSC

From our dedicated experts in our offices around the world to our extensive shipping network, we have the scale and experience to support your international fresh vegetable shipments.

In addition, we also have a full portfolio of dedicated solutions designed to make everything from shipping potatoes to shipping carrots easier and more efficient for your business.

Reefer Cargo Technology

Ship your vegetable cargo safely with our cutting-edge reefer technology. We use Controlled Atmosphere technologies, like StarCool® CA, XtendFRESH®, Liventus®, Maxtend®, and Purfresh®, to help extend the shelf life and freshness of your produce. Now you can also combine it with our iReefer solution, the most advanced container monitoring system for your reefer cargo.

Dehumidification Technology

To offer you the right solution, all our containers are equipped with humidity sensors and adjustable ventilation. These features help manage humidity—crucial for preventing excess moisture that can cause mould or dryness that can dehydrate your cargo. While the vent settings also enable proper airflow, maintaining the ideal environment to preserve freshness throughout the journey.

Read more

Year-round Support

Our team of more than 1,000 reefer experts are also on hand to provide year-round support. From peak season shipping to helping you capitalize on  demand spikes; we create tailor-made solutions that are designed to meet the specific needs of your cargo.

Did you know?

Dehumidification is particularly important for onions, ginger and garlic.

Because you Need more than
Port-to-Port Shipping

To support all your shipping needs and help you deliver your vegetable cargo to your customers as quickly and efficiently as possible, we offer you flexible and efficient inland transportation solutions, offering you door-to-door delivery solutions. Beyond this, with our cargo cover solutions we ensure you’re protected from the potential financial losses which may occur during transportation due to unexpected events like fire. Whether you’re worried about loss or damage, we work to give you the ultimate peace of mind that your cargo is in the best hands possible.

By partnering with our team, you’ll have access to the expert advice and specialized equipment you need to streamline your supply chain and consistently deliver top-quality produce to your customers.

Our range of solutions includes:

FAQs

Can you ship fresh vegetables?

Yes! Our advanced reefer technology and strict temperature and humidity controls mean we can ship fresh vegetables worldwide whilst maintaining quality and freshness.

How do you import vegetables?

To import vegetables, you’ll need to ensure all necessary documentation and certifications (including phytosanitary certificates) are complete, and that your cargo meets the import country’s regulations. Partnering with an experienced shipping company like MSC can help support you through the customs process and provide end-to-end transportation services.

How are fresh vegetables transported?

Fresh vegetables are typically transported in refrigerated (reefer) containers that maintain the ideal temperature and humidity levels.

How do you package fresh vegetables?

Fresh vegetables are usually packaged in ventilated, food-grade crates, cartons, or trays that protect them during transport while allowing airflow. Packaging may vary based on the type of vegetable, transport duration, and destination requirements.

What is the best way to transport vegetables?

Using a controlled cold chain which utilizes reefer containers. This approach ensures consistent temperature and humidity for your cargo, helping to minimize the risk of spoilage and preserving freshness, texture, and nutritional value.

Minerals and Mining Shipment FAQs

What challenges do you face with mineral and mining product transportation?

The process of organizing mining and mineral shipments can be complicated by several factors.

One of these is the many different regulations and documents that all products must be compliant with. Not only do these vary depending on the region but can also change depending on our customer requirements. To avoid delays or fines, all documentation must be accurate, which is where partnering with an expert in mining and mineral shipping solutions, like MSC, can be hugely beneficial.

Another challenge faced when shipping mineral or mining commodities is the need for additional safety and security to ensure your cargo arrives at its intended destination in good condition. Ensuring you have the right containers and storage facilities is a key part of achieving this.

Share
Link copied!

What types of mining and mineral commodities can be shipped?

Common examples of mining and mineral commodities that can be shipped include:

• Metals such as aluminium, copper, iron, ore, railway track, slag, steel, tin, or zinc

• Minerals including coal, coking coal, graphite, marble, stones

Share
Link copied!

Which is the right container for mining and mineral shipments?

For ease of handling, metal and mineral cargo can be exported in a standard container. This method is ideal for smaller quantities, valuable commodities, or materials like ore that require special handling.

Other options for shipping your metal or mineral exports with MSC include:

• Ideal for shipping hazardous, or precious cargo our dry cargo containers come in standard sizes, including 20- and 40-foot containers.

• Our specialist cargo solutions, including breakbulk and out of gauge cargo solutions are perfect for businesses needing to ship cargo that includes oversized items or that requires top-loading. Another form of project cargo solutions, MSC’s flat rack containers are designed to make shipping heavy or bulky cargo simpler and easier thanks to their collapsible sides.

Share
Link copied!

Why is it important to properly package minerals and mining cargo properly?

As some exports are corrosive, flammable, or can be affected by moisture or temperature changes, it’s vital to ensure they are packaged appropriately to prevent damage or depreciation during transit.

Share
Link copied!

What regulations and permits are required for shipping minerals internationally?

Although the regulations and documentation needed for shipping minerals internationally can vary, there are some crucial regulations that must be followed.

• All exports must include the export licensing and certificate.

• You should also check the customs tariffs and instructions of duty for your country of import

• You may also need to confirm what the aggregate levy and climate change levy is for your import and exports.

Our global teams of industry experts are on hand to help advise and support you on which documentation you need for your mineral export.

Share
Link copied!

Which country produces the most minerals?

The top countries known for producing the most mineral exports include:

• Zimbabwe

• Gabon

• The Democratic Republic of Congo

• Egypt

• Libya

• Angola

• Algeria

• Nigeria

• South Africa

Why Trust your Pharmaceutical Shipments to MSC?

How are Pharmaceutical Products Transported?

Pharmaceutical cargo is transported in temperature-controlled reefer containers which allow the consistent management of conditions throughout transportation. At MSC our reefer containers use the most advanced cooling systems, including:

Primeline®

Naturaline®

Star Cool SA

These systems ensure that pharmaceutical products are kept at the required temperature during transit, while dehumidification systems prevent damage or degradation. We also use the latest green technology in our fleet to help minimize your supply chain’s carbon footprint.

GDP Compliant Practices

Because of the sensitive nature of the cargo, the shipping of pharmaceuticals needs to be well organised, and best practices adhered to.

Our GDP certification ensures that our processes are aligned with the strict regulations required by the pharma industry. With MSC, your cargo is in the hands of dedicated experts who are trained to offer the right support, advice and documentation whenever and wherever it is needed.

Local Experts Around the World

Work with local experts around the world, all of whom have a deep knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry. Not only do we have more than five decades of experience carrying sensitive and hazardous cargo, but our global contacts will be on hand to help throughout your cargo’s journey, with the ability to support container preparation and packing if necessary.

Door-to-door Security

Safety is paramount for the transportation of pharma cargo, which is often highly valuable. Our containers are sealed and locked from pick-up to delivery, and our door-to-door services minimize touchpoints – helping to improve product quality and integrity, and reduce the risk of theft or damage.

We follow highly standardized control procedures to guarantee optimal transport conditions.

Learn More About our Solutions
Download our brochure

Healthcare Logistics

On land and at sea, we have everything you need to prepare your pharma logistics and supply chain securely from A to Z.

To ensure vaccines and medications are delivered without spoilage, pharma, and healthcare logistics require complete legislative adherence. As well as providing a temperature-monitored pharma supplied chain, at MSC we can also provide support for other healthcare logistics throughout your supply chain by acting as 2PL, 3PL, or 4PL as required.

Questions about our Pharma Logistics Solutions?

We've got you covered

Important aspects to consider in pharmaceutical shipping

Along with following best practices within the pharmaceutical industry throughout the entire shipping process, there are several important regulations to follow during the transportation process. These include:

• Ensuring all pharma products are properly packaged and labelled. This mitigates the risk of any cargo breaking or becoming damaged during transit. Having clear labels on products also means that correct temperatures can be monitored and maintained during shipping.

• Licensing regulations. As there are certain licensing requirements needed to ship pharmaceuticals, it is crucial to work with a company like MSC that holds all the necessary licenses.

• The hygiene of shipping facilities. As well as being kept to the required temperate, all containers and storage facilities involved in transporting pharmaceuticals must be large enough in order to allow proper cleaning and airflow to take place shape.

At MSC we work hard to consider all aspects of pharmaceutical transportation, from the industry regulations we follow to our reefer container systems and shipping processes.

Share
Link copied!

How are you usually audited to be GDP compliant (Goods Distribution Practice)?

Our GDP certification is supported by mandatory internal and external audits. We go through an intense 1st, 2nd and 3rd party audit program, where we audit ourselves (1st party), our vendors and suppliers (2nd party) and we have an external certified body auditing our system (3rd party).

Each audit checks the following elements of our suppliers’ processes and systems:

- Documents are verified – documental verification of our GDP system.

- On-site inspections are carried out.

- Calibrations are verified.

- Traceability testing is checked.

- The CAPA (Corrective Action and Preventative Actions) Management process is reviewed.

- Overall system performance is reviewed and improvements are planned.

Share
Link copied!

How is quality measured?

Performance metrics for our GDP practices are overseen by several departments within MSC to ensure quality, including:

- Customer Services (Agencies level).

- Reefer Management (SSC Antwerp).

- Claims Dept MSC HQ (Geneva).

- Under Penalty Cargo (SSC Greece).

Share
Link copied!

Do you carry out CAPA (Corrective Action and Preventative Actions) procedures?

Yes. In order to be GDP compliant, we have an internal CAPA management process. CAPA management is internally shared, and its performances are periodically reviewed.

Share
Link copied!

Where can I find documentation?

All relevant documents are available from your local pharma expert, contact your local MSC office for more information.

Share
Link copied!

Are MSC staff GDP Trained?

MSC staff involved in GDP / FSM undergo in-person or online training relevant to their roles, including reefer handling and maintenance, alarms and incident management and CAPA management.

Attendance to these training programs is both mandatory and verified.

Share
Link copied!

How are containers cleaned in order to be GDP compliant?

This is overseen by our Reefer department in Geneva and Antwerp.

They also oversee training practices for cleaning and adherence to high cleaning standards, according to the container and cargo needs.

Specific audits are planned and carried out globally to verify the adherence of our vendors to our GDP standards.

Share
Link copied!

Is the container temperature controlled?

Yes! All these procedures are part of our ISO 22000 audit and part of our general GDP practices.

We have departments dedicated to handling temperature-controlled units, both in Geneva and in our main facilities. All agencies have departments dedicated to temperature-controlled containers, with professionals available in each facility trained in pre-trip, and handling alarms etc.

Each vessel is equipped with essential spare parts in line with the type of equipment loaded.

Share
Link copied!

How is temperature monitored?

The temperature monitoring is regulated by the Service Contract Agreement with Vessels/Ports and Facilities and includes a minimum of two controls per day. Alerts are raised if a unit is out of an acceptable range.

For GDP units, the range of acceptance is ‘Zero Deviation’ from requirements. For specific cargo-loading plan-routing, temperature mapping is agreed with the shipper.

Share
Link copied!

Are MSC containers’ temperature sensors calibrated?

Calibration of thermal sensors is ensured by the certification of the constructor and suppliers of spare parts.

In addition, MSC tests has a specific procedure to verify the calibration of the units and a specific audit program to verify that unit probes are correctly calibrated.

Share
Link copied!

Is my cargo safe?

MSC’s security divisions maintain and audit cargo according to the highest standards and requirement of the US Customs and Border Patrol (USCBP). A Seal Management plan runs through the organization and involves all offices and depots across the company.

Our safe cargo checks are in line with ISO 28000:2007 certification.

Share
Link copied!

Do you work with certified suppliers?

With all our main vendors handling temperature-controlled containers, like ports and depot facilities, we have specific clauses in place for handling special cargo, including pharmaceuticals.

Audit operations are performed and verified by our Procurement department and are in line with our ISO 28000:2017 certification, our GDP 2013 and GDP 2015 certification and with ISO 22000: 2018.

Safely Ship Manufacturing Materials

Transported to and from every major trade lane, plastic and rubber goods are at the very centre of most modern global supply chains. Plastic and rubber comes in all shapes and sizes, from raw materials to finished items. MSC ship plastics, natural rubber and rubber products all around the world.

From natural polymers to petrochemical derivatives and thermoplastics, these commodities are essential to the manufacture, processing or packaging of products across countless other industries. There is also a substantial industry in the responsible recycling of plastics, rubber and scrap materials, and MSC plays a key role in the management and safe transport of these by-products to safe recycling destinations.

Why Trust your Plastics and Rubber Shipments to MSC?

Is it Dangerous to Ship Plastics and Rubber?

If managed efficiently, the shipping process for plastics and rubber products is entirely safe. Ethylene and propylene are transported as small plastic pellets, which are bagged and moved to and from ports and over sea in either our 20 foot or 40 foot steel containers. Polyethylene resin can be transported by truck, barge or train safely to manufacturing facilities to make end products.

Global Coverage and Local Expertise

Our 675 global offices are staffed with experienced, knowledgeable teams ready to provide expert guidance on shipping your plastic or rubber products both locally and globally. Our experts with a detailed understanding of the procedures needed when shipping plastics and rubber, will ensure that your cargo is transported in a way that meets industry standards and reduces risk to a minimum.

Customer Service Tailored to your Needs

What consistently sets MSC apart is our outstanding customer service. We work hard to build productive relationships with our customers, taking time to get to know their business properly; that way we’re able to offer flexible solutions that reflect their changing needs.

Make MSC your Plastics and Rubber Partner

Successfully servicing the huge demand for plastics and rubber materials requires a shipping and logistics operation on a global scale, as well as expert knowledge of the sector. That is why so many of the world’s leading plastic and rubber companies choose MSC as their transport partner.

To find out more about our plastics and rubber shipping service, please get in touch with us today

FAQs About Shipping Wood Products?

How is wood pulp shipped?

Wood pulp is packaged into pressed bales and can either be shipped ‘wet’ or ‘dry’. Similarly, to the final paper products, wood pulp is also sensitive to the effects of moisture, and changes in humidity can cause it to swell or decay during transport. At MSC we ensure that an appropriate temperature is maintained, and changes in humidity are avoided throughout the pulp shipping process.

How is wood shipped?

MSC have experts in shipping logs and wood ready to help you save time and simplify your supply chain during wood shipping.

To prevent any contamination, we provide dedicated cargo fumigation services for wood shipment. Our full portfolio of solutions make use of market-leading global port coverage, and extensive availability as well as digital solutions. All of this ensures we deliver fast and reliable transit times for your wood exports.

To find out if our fumigation services are available in your region enquire today.

Forestry in Canada: The 3 Logistical Keys for Exporting

With $17.1 billion of its net trade attributed to the export of forestry products, Canada has established itself as a global leader in the forestry export market. Not only does Canada hold the largest share of the global NBSK (Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft) market, but they are also known as a major producer and exporter of softwood lumber.

Forming Strong Roots in the Forestry Sector

Pulp, paper, and forestry goods are a notable part of the cargo that MSC carries all around the world. For example, in Scandinavia, the Baltic states and Central Europe, some countries’ exports are made up of up to 50% of this type of cargo. As well as within Europe, we have a strong global presence within the industry through our offices in key regions such as Asia, Africa and the Americas.

Retail

Count on us for Retail Shipping and Logistics

Whether it’s shipping white goods, apparel shipping, or shipping shoes today retail success depends on business’s being able to efficiently source and ship products, all while maintaining a “just-in-time” supply chain that is flexible and robust.

To help you deliver exceptional products to your customers, our retail shipping experts provide seamless and reliable port-to-port delivery for retailers of every size. With dedicated services from Asia to key Western markets, and integrated inland and digital solutions, you have full visibility and control across your retail supply chain. While we take care of logistics, you can stay focused on what matters most, providing high-quality products your customers trust and return for.

When shipping furniture, home decor, beauty products, or fast-moving consumer goods (FMCGs), you can rely on MSC and leverage our growing number of ocean services and dedicated full portfolio of solutions.

Why Choose MSC For Your Retail Logistics

Beyond our experience in retail shipping, our customer support team works to understand the individual needs of your business. As a result, we can design and deliver services that meet your particular cargo requirements.

Fast and Reliable Transit Times

Our extensive network, including our East-West routes allows us to deliver your cargo anywhere in the world quickly and efficiently.

Combined with our road and rail inland shipping solutions, all your key stakeholders remain connected across your supply chain, helping you deliver your goods on time, every time.

Extensive Inventory of Equipment

Whether you need GOH for shipping clothes, reefer containers for FMCGs, or food grade containers to preserve the quality of your cargo throughout transportation, partnering with MSC will give you access to an extensive array of well-maintained equipment that will protect your retail cargo from start to finish.

Learn more

Delivering the Best with our
Digital Solutions

From our eBL solution to myMSC ebusiness platform, or our iReefer solution, we continually invest in our digital solutions. This provides you with greater insight into your cargo’s condition, as well as additional insight to help improve your supply chain planning and optimization.

Fun Fact

MSC Gülsün could hold the equivalent of 1,995,504 washing machines – that’s almost 2 million!

Let MSC Look after your Retail Shipments

Leverage MSC for retail exports and imports. We understands that logistics can be a major challenge for retail companies. That is why our growing number of ocean services and value-added shipping solutions offer the perfect fit for retail imports and exports.

Our customer support team will take the time to understand your individual needs in order to design and deliver services that supports you as your business and product lines evolve.

Comprehensive network of global services. We ship from all major retail producing regions, to more than 150 nations.

Dedicated retail solutions. Our value-added services include GOH, warehousing and intermodal equipment and solutions (availability depends on selected agencies).

Track retail shipments overseas remotely. Our smart containers provide timely information for better planning and decision making.

Access the scale, speed and reliability that you deserve. MSC’s East-West Network offers more ports, more weekly departures, faster transit times and improved reliability.

Because you Need more than
Port-to-Port Shipping

Our experience shipping retail cargo, combined with our wealth on inland and digital solutions means our team can offer you tailored solutions to suit your specific supply chain demands. This leaves you free to focus on continually delivering high quality products to your customers.

Fashion moves at a rapid pace, with different seasons and trends forcing businesses involved in the industry to quickly adapt their products to capitalize on customer demand. This high-speed turnover means that for companies to succeed in the industry, they need to be able to deliver high-quality products to their customers at pace. In turn, this puts increasing pressure on factories, suppliers, distributors, retailers and warehouses to deliver either completed products, or the necessary components to create the required apparel cargo.

High competition levels, combined with changing customer expectations, can be challenging. That’s why working with a shipping company that can deliver quick and reliable apparel shipping could be what sets apart your fashion business from your competition.

Working with MSC means you’ll be able to utilize our global presence and decades of industry experience to full effect and ensure that your apparel supply chain operates at maximum efficiency.

Why Trust your Apparel Shipments to MSC?

GOH Equipment for Shipping Clothing

No one likes wrinkled clothes at the best of times. Now you can avoid this problem and expedite the unloading process by utilizing our dedicated clothing shipping solution your fashion and apparel shipping.

Available across specific routes* MSC’s garment-on-hanger (GOH) containers* – or ‘hangtainers’ are designed to safely and conveniently transport clothing garments on hangers. This service saves you both time, labour, and money when moving garments from container to shop floor as well as ensuring your fashion cargo arrives at its final destination in the best possible condition.

*subject to availability- please check with your local agency

Read more

Cutting-Edge Digital Solutions for Fashion Shipping

The speed of the market makes investing in digitalization vital for businesses operating in the retail industry.

Partnering with MSC allows you to utilize services such as our eBL solution, and smart container tracking. This increased visibility of your retail cargo means you’ll continually be able to meet and manage expectations and consistently provide the best possible experience for your customers.

As well as our digital solutions, you’ll also be able to simplify and optimize your shipping process with our eBusiness platform myMSC where you can complete your business transactions in a few clicks.

Read more

Speedy Solutions for Your Apparel Shipping Needs

Whether it’s for a certain event, or because of a new trend, your customers want their recent purchases as quickly as possible.

Our global sea and inland transportation network, enables us to simplify your apparel supply chain by providing flexible end-to-end solutions. Customizable to your needs, MSC’s dedicated solutions help ensure that your supply chain will operate as efficiently as possible, helping you and your customers to stay on trend!

Because you Need more than
Port-to-Port Services

MSC’s extensive shipping network connects the largest exporting markets worldwide, including China, Southeast Asia, the US, the EU and the Indian Subcontinent, to every corner of the world.

Our modern, efficient fleet also calls at 520 ports on 300 routes. Not only does this help support your production cycles, but also means you’ll consistently meet your time-to-market requirements, helping you generate increased customer loyalty and a positive brand reputation.

Speed, efficiency, and visibility are vital for businesses looking to thrive in the fashion industry. Collaborating with our teams of industry experts for your apparel exports to utilize our digital and bespoke solutions helps ensure that your supply chain is as efficient as possible. Cosmetics Supply Chain and Shipping Beauty Products With MSC

As cosmetics products have become more and more sophisticated, the cosmetics industry itself has been ever-growing and expanding.

While some are classed as pharmaceutical products, cosmetics cover everything from lotions and body creams to perfume, shower gel, makeup, face creams, and shampoos. The diversity of the products being shipped means that it’s vital to work with a shipping partner who has the scale and global network to support your cosmetics supply chain.

MSC is your sure partner for your cosmetic and beauty product distribution thanks to our range of specialist equipment. Including dry and reefer cargo, our range of shipping solutions is designed to suit your cosmetic product exports.

Beyond this, our fleet of modern, clean, and fuel-efficient vessels can help you to reduce your supply chain's carbon footprint. All our equipment is well-maintained so you can rest assured that your cosmetics cargo is in safe hands.

Why Trust your Cosmetics Shipments to MSC?

Supporting Your Cosmetics Supply Chain

Whether you’re shipping skincare or hair products, having a seamless cosmetics supply chain is vital for ensuring customer satisfaction and a positive brand reputation.

Our full portfolio of solutions means you’ll access to a range of solutions across your entire cosmetics supply chain, helping to improve its overall efficiency. This helps improve your overall planning and strategic approach to your cosmetics exports, enhancing the accuracy of your operations and increasing your profits.

Digital Solutions for Your Cosmetics Shipment

Beyond this, our range of digital solutions offer greater security, transparency, and efficiency throughout your cosmetics export.

At MSC, we continuously invest in our digital shipping solutions to offer the very best visibility and services for our customers. Whether it’s our electronic bill of lading (eBL), direct integrations, or smart containers, we aim to provide enhanced visibility and greater supply chain management for your cosmetics business.

Advice from Local Experts

Throughout your cosmetic cargo’s journey, our team of experts will work with you to understand the specific needs of your business and offer you advice for the best shipping or inland transportation solutions to meet your requirements.

Equally, we work to provide a single point of contact for each shipment. This enhanced communication means you can be sure of a reliable and fully optimized supply chain.

Managing Your Cosmetics Exports

Used for cleansing, protecting, and moisturizing, it’s important to ensure that your cosmetics exports are kept at the correct temperature to maintain their quality and integrity throughout transportation. Other considerations for your cosmetics exports include:

Implementing robust quality control measurements ahead of shipping

Ensuring that all regulatory requirements are met

Using appropriate packaging and labelling to minimize potential damage during shipping

At MSC, our global network, combined with our cold chain logistics solutions for shipping beauty products, is designed to offer you peace of mind throughout transportation. For reliable shipping, global network coverage, fast transit times, and exceptional customer support discover our full range of services now.

FAQs About White Goods & Electronics?

What is the difference between white goods and household appliances?

While the term ‘white goods’ can sometimes refer to white fabrics, typically, when talking about shipping, ‘white goods’ are usually defined as large home appliances. These include stoves, refrigerators, freezers, washing machines, tumble dryers, dishwashers, and air conditioners.

White goods are one of the main categories of household appliances. The other categories of household appliances include:

Consumer electronics (also known as brown goods) such a computers, radios, or games consoles.

Small appliances like toasters, coffee makers, and blenders.

Share
Link copied!

How are white goods cargo best stored?

To avoid damage caused by damp weather radiation, contamination, or theft, household appliances should be securely stored inside a warehouse.

At MSC, our global network of cargo storage solutions helps ensure the smooth transportation of your white goods and consumer electronics from start to finish. Our dry storage warehousing network is designed to help you maximize efficiency throughout your supply chain and ensure your cargo remains undamaged during transportation.

Share
Link copied!

How are household appliances packaged for transportation?

Because of their value and usefulness as a commodity, all white goods and consumer electronics shipments must be treated with care throughout their transportation journey.

Before shipping, household appliances are packaged in cartons manufactured from millboard, corrugated board, wooden, or plywood boxes using paperboard. Internally, all corners are covered using edge protectors and the cargo is surrounded by plastic materials (airbags, bubble wrap, or moldings) to protect against impact and avoid damage.

Any electronics or white goods that have scratch sensitive materials are further protected by plastic film, foam sheets, or tissue paper to further ensure that they arrive in good condition. Similarly, large appliances that will need to be manually handled during transportation are packaged into cartons that align with the appliance’s centre of gravity. This improves stability and prevents injury during handling.

Our teams of experts understand all the intricate details that come with packaging and shipping large electronics and white goods. We provide thorough checks throughout the packaging process to ensure that all packaging openings are completely closed, and your cargo is properly protected.

Share
Link copied!

White goods and home appliances transportation best practices

When it comes to white goods and consumer electronics shipments, we are industry leaders. This is due to our commitment to following best practices throughout the transportation of your household appliance shipment. We use world-class dry shipping containers to ensure that your cargo arrives safely at its final destination and that your overall supply chain remains undisrupted.

Other best practice guidelines that must be followed when transporting white goods and consumer electronics include:

Performing surveys during the packing and unpacking stages and certificates issued.

Ensuring all cargo is secured (for example by interlocking stowage) in the area by the container door.

Protecting goods on all sides (floor, sides, top) with dunnage.

Suspending a nonwoven fabric in the container during shipments through various climatic regions to protect the cargo from dripping water or condensation.

Marking all cargo with the appropriate transport markings such as ‘handle with care’, ‘fragile’, ‘keep dry’ to ensure its safety.

Key International Shipping Regions

Alongside our wealth of shipping and logistics solutions, our global shipping network also encompasses numerous trade routes and key regions.

Shipping to Europe

Whether you’re shipping to or shipping from Europe, or looking to enhance your intra-European trade, we have the size and experience to support your needs. Leverage on our network of services which includes our Short Sea Network for efficient ocean transport within Europe, the East-West Network which connects key ports in all regions and our Transatlantic Network for your European exports to Americas and enjoy an end-to-end shipping experience.

Shipping in Africa

Our Africa shipping services cover over 45 countries, enabling our teams to offer you detailed advice from anywhere on the continent. Our strong intermodal solutions also mean that we have become a key part of the supply chain for numerous businesses importing or exporting their goods from Africa.

America Shipping

When it comes to shipping in America, the size and scale of our operations means that we can offer dedicated solutions across both North and South America.

Whether you’re shipping from North America and looking for support with shipping mineral and mining or forestry cargo, or for coffee exports in South America, our team has the experience you need to find the best solutions for you.

Asia Pacific Shipping

To support businesses shipping to or from the Asia Pacific region, we have our dedicated East-West Network and other services that cover all major shipping lanes from Southwest Asia and Oceania.

Not only will you have the support of our local teams, but also their experience and knowledge to ensure we find the best solutions for your business.

Shipping in the Middle East

Our Middle East Shipping solutions are designed to support businesses shipping everything from oil, to plastics, and fertilizers. Not only do we ship across numerous routes, but our presence across key ports including the Port of Jebel Ali and Salalah enables us to deliver efficient transportation services that ensure your cargo reaches its final destination quickly and safely.

Tools

Wherever you’re shipping from, partnering with MSC and our global shipping network means that you’ll have a team of experts by your side throughout your cargo’s journey. From finding the best shipping solutions to offering guidance through cargo insurance and customs clearance, we will be with you every step of the way. Contact our teams of expert or take advantage of our online tools.

Shipping in Africa: our Key Offerings

As well as offering global port coverage, at MSC our regular shipping solutions to and from Africa are linked by regional feeder services and strong inland transportation resources. This enables us to effectively connect landlocked countries and remote areas to ports and global commercial centres. Furthermore, our integrated road and rail transport solutions have enabled us to become the supply chain partner for numerous businesses importing and exporting from Africa.

Whether you’re looking for dry, reefer, liquid, or project cargo shipping solutions, our decades of experience means we have an array of shipping solutions designed to meet the needs of your business.

Beyond this, our trade managers have an in-depth understanding of individual overseas markets and the dynamics of specific trades. Because of this, we can offer market-specific, local advice on factors affecting the transit of any type of cargo being shipped from Africa, such as:

• Terminal conditions

• Local or overseas transport infrastructure

• Berthing delays or congestion

• Local or overseas regulatory and political changes

• Relevant customs procedures

Inland Services

As well as offering high-quality ocean freight services, by partnering with MSC you’ll also have access to our wealth of intermodal and haulage services. Not only does this enable door-to-door delivery for your cargo, but this level of global connectivity is designed to enhance your overall supply chain and make your African exports and imports as efficient as possible.

Our intermodal offerings are further supported by our network of warehouses, enabling us to provide comprehensive storage and packing facilities. For businesses located in South Africa, we also offer cold storage solutions, designed to further enhance your cold chain logistics solutions.

Digital Solutions

At MSC, we believe that digitalization has the power to make shipping in Africa more efficient, secure, and sustainable. Because of this, we continuously invest in new tools and technologies that are designed to provide you with easy-to-use, flexible, and reliable online shipping management solutions. Our digital solutions include:

myMSC, our official 24/7 eBusiness platform.

MSC eBL, designed to offer a more efficient, secure, and sustainable way of processing your Bill of Lading (BL).

API (Application Programming Interface) and EDI (Electronic Data Interchange)

Smart Containers so you have real-time information about your freight anytime, anywhere.

Cargo Cover Solutions

Shipping cargo internationally can be stressful for everyone involved. That’s why, we designed our Cargo Cover solutions to provide you with the widest possible coverage for maritime and inland transportation.

As part of our Cargo Cover solutions, our local offices will take care of the entire process for you, from initial quotation to fast claim resolution.

Significant Shipping Ports in Africa

For businesses shipping to Africa, or looking to export their cargo quickly and easily, working with MSC means you’ll have access to all major ports in the region, including:

Port of Mombasa, Kenya

Port of Durban, South Africa

Port of Lagos (Tincan/Lagos), Nigeria

Dar-es-Salaam Port, Tanzania

Port of Abidjan, Ivory Coast

Port of Beira, Mozambique

Port of Walvis Bay, Namibia

Port of Djibouti, Republic of Djibouti

Fostering Inclusive Trade

Alongside our commitment to our customers, at MSC we are also committed to ensuring a positive social impact wherever we operate. We invest locally to enable economic development across the entire African continent. This includes:

● Recruiting a local workforce and supporting employees to develop their careers.

● Facilitating maritime trade to tackle food insecurity.

● Investing in infrastructure to improve connections.

● Assisting in the development of international trade.

● Creating new opportunities for small farmers.

● Providing access to our global shipping network.

VGM receiving policy in Gabon

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in Gabon are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

Submission Date

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC : first create the myMSC account and gain access and assistance to follow up the procedure (Free of Charge)

EDI (via IBOX _ only for MSC interns)

Manually (via IBOX _ only for MSC interns)

Email: CustomerServices@msc.com / GA671-DocumentationExport@msc.com

Guidelines for submitting VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered.

Any Shipper of Record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal.

All rail shipments must have the VGM submitted within 24 hours of the container gating in at the origin rail ramp, to avoid any extra fees levied by the terminal for weighing services. Late gates will only be considered for approval when a VGM is submitted by the Shipper of Record before 12:00 noon, local time, on the day of the cargo cut-off.

Note: locally, clients consume very much less that 24 hours in the submission of their VGMs.

MSC admin fees and costs

Manual VGM Submission Fee (applies to email, fax, and inclusion on standard shipping instructions).

Late VGM Submission Fee.

VGM Misdeclaration Fee.

NB: locally the fees and costs are not rightly implemented (some technical adaptations still ongoing); per different situations/cases, applicable to Client is defined.

Questions about VGM?

Contact our Customer Service team - CustomerServices@msc.com / GA671-DocumentationExport@msc.com.

Additional information

Additional information

Bills of Lading (BLs) function as a receipt of freight services, a contract between a freight carrier and shipper, and a document of title. The BL is a legally binding document that provides the details needed to process the freight shipment and invoice it correctly. In Gabon, BLs must be endorsed by shippers and a local Notify (see below) with a Gabonese address.

Restrictions & Requirements:

- For car/vehicle shipments to Libreville, it is mandatory to include the year (must be less than 5 years), brand and full chassis number.

- For cargo in transit, the BL and cargo manifest must include "Cargo in Transit To".

- The BIETC number must be included in all matters related to split BL.

- BL numbers with a letter at the end (usually an A) are no longer allowed by Customs. However, two or more BLS covering a single container are allowed as long as the numbers are clearly different.

Customs fines: Any Manifest corrector requested after vessel arrival or less than 72h before vessel arrival is subject to customs fines of USD 120 in addition to USD 60 for the documentation fee. Any Change of Destination for shipments booked from all ports to Libreville are subject to MSC Gabon’s approval for BIETC number checking and customs acceptance.

Manifest correctors: Any Manifest corrector regarding weight/packages and description less than 72 hours before vessel arrival are subject to a documentation fee of USD 60 plus USD 120 per customs amendment. However, changes to Shipper/Consignee/Notify after manifest validation are no longer allowed. In addition, any amendment/modification that may lead to additional fees are imparted not to the Port of Discharge , but to the request agency. For more information, email GA671-DocumentationExport@msc.com.

Manifest deadlines: For all cargo to Gabon, a DTX file from the last transhipment port should be sent 24 hours prior to the vessel’s arrival.

Prohibited goods: The following goods are not authorized for shipments in Gabon: nuclear/radioactive products, waste, logs or vehicles over five years old (legislative decree n° 0551/PR/MTL only authorize the importation of vehicles aged less than five years). In case of non-compliance, cargo will be rejected by local authorities and agent(s) at POL will be responsible for any costs incurred. If you have any queries, please email GA671-documentationImport@msc.com or GA671-salesgabon@msc.com.

Telex release: refers to a message that is sent by an agent or shipping line from the origin to the office at the customs destination. It can also be sent from an agent to signify that the shipper has already surrendered the O/BL issued to them. For help, contact: telexreleasegabon@mscga.mscgva.ch

Weight limitations are subject to container payload, while overweight and oversize are subject to management’s approval.

Country-specific customs regulations:

BIETC (cargo tracking number): A BIETC is mandatory for all cargo from or to Gabon. Visit www.cgcworld.com for a usage guide and https://bietc.cgcworld.com to register for an ID.

Certificate of conformity (CoC): A CoC has been mandatory for all shipments to Gabon since 2016. As CoCs are required for customs clearance, any cargo arriving in Gabon without the corresponding CoC will not be permitted to enter the country.

Reefer cargo: For all information regarding plugging, please visit this website.

Notify party: any shipment from Gabon must have a Notify party with an address in Gabon and a valid phone/fax number.

UAC: Cargo that is not cleared after three months is systematically seized and auctioned without notice.

Cut-off dates

Cut-off dates

The cut-off date is the last date that the container can be returned to the port terminal to meet the schedule.

For standard and reefer containers, the cut-off period is the same: 48 hours before arrival at berth.

The cut-off for VGM is 48 hours after arrival at berth.

VGM (Verified Gros Mass): Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

VGM cut-off: the cut-off value is 48 hours after arrival at Berth.

Connecting Gambia to the world

MSC  Gambia has been helping customers to ship their cargo worldwide since 2010. Today, one of the leading shipping companies in The Gambia, MSC Gambia can ship more than 4,000 TEUS annually to destinations around the world.

Groundnuts, sesame, cashew nuts, scrap metals, and fish and seafood products are the main export commodities from the Gambia, with most of them destined for the Far East, India, the EU and the US.

The country’s main imports are mostly finished products and foodstuffs from the Far East, the EU, the US and other parts of the world. Given the size of the country, the bulk of these imports transit to neighboring countries.

Connecting Ghana's Trade to the World Since 1998

MSC has been proudly serving Ghana since 1998, connecting businesses to global trade through our extensive shipping and logistics network. Over the years, we have grown into one of Ghana's leading container shipping and logistics providers, supporting the transportation of key export commodities such as cocoa, cashew nuts, timber, and other strategic cargoes that drive the country's international trade.

With our Ghana headquarters in Tema and branch offices in Takoradi and Kumasi, our team of local experts delivers reliable shipping, intermodal, and supply chain solutions tailored to the needs of importers and exporters. By combining deep knowledge of the Ghanaian market with the strength of MSC's global network, we help customers move cargo efficiently and confidently to destinations around the world.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable on export containers when containers remain with customers and not returned full for export before the free days expire.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable when the free days expire on import containers until they are returned empty to our depot.

In case of a demurrage dispute, email GH526-helpdesk.tema@msc.com (with as email subject: Dispute + Invoice Number), describing the reasons for the dispute.

SOLAS VGM information for Ghana

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, we request all our export customers to provide VGM certificate before cargo is loaded. Customers use third party VGM service providers to weigh their containers.

What to include in VGM instructions

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM and weight measurement unit (lbs or kgs)

Name of responsible party

How to submit VGM instructions

VGM instructions should be submitted on myMSC (free of charge).

Prohibited cargo

As per general MSC rules and subject to the destination of the shipment, the following are prohibited:

Fireworks, ammunition, small arms

Second-hand empty gas cylinders

Frozen turkey tails

Ammonium nitrate

Second-hand mattresses

Second-hand tyres (subject to the approval of MSC Ghana)

Used refrigerators, used fridge-freezers, used freezers and used refrigeration compressors (motors)

In line with Ghana's obligations under the Montreal Protocol and The Energy Efficiency Regulations, 2008 (L.I.1932), the government of Ghana has completely banned the import of used refrigerators, used fridge-freezers, used freezers and used refrigeration compressors (motors). Booking agents should immediately stop accepting such cargo to Ghana (Tema and Takoradi) as MSC may be held responsible when discharging containers infringing the law.

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land. In case of a demurrage dispute, email GIN-info@msc.com

What is Per Diem?

A storage charge is applicable for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (to use the land) after the free time expires.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

1. Prohibition of vehicles with right hand

Pursuant to the new decree n° D/2020/298/PRG/SGG , herewith attached, with immediate effect,  pls DO NOT ACCEPT any booking for Vehicles with right hand when the POD or Final destination is Guinea.

2. Regulation of the age limit for used vehicles

As from July 15th 2021 (sailing date @ POL) it is strictly forbidden to import used vehicles older than 13 years. This applies to any          type of used vehicle (car, truck etc.)

Used vehicle must be inspected by any entity allowed to do so at origin country and that entity is required to issue a certificate or an equivalent document stating the condition of the vehicle. The certificate must be sent to consignee as it will be required during clearing formalities.

Therefore, we request POLs to inform shippers and make sure they are in full compliance with above before loading any vehicle.

Failure to comply may result in heavy fines and vehicles may be scrapped locally or reloaded back to origin at POL agent's expenses.

Things you need to know

SOLAS VGM information for Côte d'Ivoire

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in the Ivory Coast are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments. Download our Ivory Coast VGM policy and terminal guidelines for more information.

VGM Responsabilities

Container is the responsibility of the shipper and so is the information.

As a shipper, you will be responsible for providing all VGM details within myMSC booking platform. Vendors or terminal operators are responsible for only loading containers with a VGM. Find more information on Tare Weight and SOLAS VGM: https://www.msc.com/en/lp/blog/key-terms/vgm-tare-weight-guide

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

EDI (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Manually (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Email: CIV-info@msc.com (note: the email will only be monitored for VGM declarations)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered.

Any Shipper of Record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal.

For truck delivery, the ultimate deadline for VGM submission will be 12:00 noon local time on the day of the cargo cut-off.

There are currently no US terminals with a “NO VGM – No GATE” policy.

All rail shipments must have the VGM submitted within 24 hours of the container gating in at the origin rail ramp, to avoid any extra fees levied by the terminal for weighing services. Late gates will only be considered for approval when a VGM is submitted by the Shipper of Record before 12:00 noon, local time, on the day of the cargo cut-off.

MSC admin fees and costs

Manual VGM Submission Fee (applies to email, fax, and inclusion on standard shipping instructions): 25 USD per container.

Late VGM Submission Fee: 25 USD per container.

VGM Misdeclaration Fee: 300 USD per misdeclaration, per container.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge to use the carrier’s full container, inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard, after the expiry of the free time. This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing inspection by customs, or while the cargo inside the container is being reworked for safety reasons.

What are storage charges?

Storage charges are billed directly to customers by APM Terminals after free days period.

For details, visit their website

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

Detention and demurrage: updated payment policy

For immediate release, payment must be by cash, Manager's check, wire transfer.

For immediate release, payment must be deposited at Ecobank Liberia Limited via direct deposit or transfer.

If the payment cannot be made by direct deposit, or transfer, payment by cheque is acceptable. However, the shipment will be released ONLY after the funds clear.

Questions about detention, demurrage, Per Diem?

Contact our Liberia team.

Link copied!

SOLAS VGM information

What is VGM?

Verified gross mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

The following are included on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM and weight measurement unit (lbs or kgs)

Name of responsible party

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in CAPITAL LETTERS.

Exporters can sign myMSC to upload the VGM.

VGM should be provided 24 hours prior vessel arrival to avoid late fees of USD25.00.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

· Container number

myMSC (Free of Charge)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo, which will be billed to the Shipper of Record.

SOLAS VGM information for Mauritius

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, Port Louis terminal is now allowed to use their certified scales to record shipment VGM.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM and weight measurement unit (kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before planning containers on the vessel. This helps to be sure that VGM details are well submitted before loading containers.

The ultimate deadline for VGM submission is three days before vessel arrival.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is Demurrage & Detention?

Demurrage & Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container.

At Import

The period of freetime starts as of the day of discharge from the vessel at terminal and ends the day of the empty container drop off.

At Export

The period of freetime starts as of the day of empty container release and ends the day of the commercial proforma date – ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) communicated during your booking – of selected vessel. If the loading vessel changes upon customer’s request, the application the application period begins when the empty equipment is picked-up and stops the day of loading on board vessel.

Share
Link copied!

SOLAS VGM information

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

Government approval status

The French government has published since May 28th 2016 a decree with tolerance 5% inaccuracy allowed on two methods.

What to include in your VGM instructions

The following items are mandatory and must be in all VGM instructions :

Booking number or B/L number

The container number

The VGM in kg

The name of the responsible person in capital

letters, as electronic equivalent of the signature

How to submit your VGM instructions

myMSC.com

EDI (via INTTRA, GT NEXUS, Cargo Smart and any other)

Shipping instructions signed

Fax, email

Deadlines for sending your VGM instructions

VGM must be known to the ship-agent, at least 24 hours before physical closing of the vessel.

The VGM cut-off date will be mentioned on the booking confirmation. If the VGM is received later, the container will not be planned / loaded on the vessel.

Admin Fees and costs

If the VGM has to be handled manually by the local agent, a local fee of 100€ per container will be applied. This also applies for VGM info added in the electronic booking.

If the VGM is not received before VGM closing time, container will be put on hold and all related costs like demurrage, storage, moves, plugging… will be for the account of the shipper.

If the VGM declaration is wrong after loading on board, a penalty will occured of 500€ per container, extracost and collateral expenses will be invoiced.

Contact information

Email: FR147-vgm.france@msc.com

Tel: + (33) 2.32.74.68.00

Link copied!

LOI (Letter of indemnity) for lost or destroyed OBLs (Original Bills of Lading)

What is an LOI?

An LOI (Letter of Indeminity) is required when an original Bill of Lading is lost or destroyed. It can be completed by shipper at the Port of Loading, or by the consignee at the Port of Discharge.

The LOI requires 200% of the commercial value of the cargo plus Ocean Freight to be guaranteed either through bank or MSC’s Insurance company.

MSC’s global LOI requirements are set out by our Geneva headquarters. The LOI must be completed as per these instructions in order for a duplicate Bill of Lading to be issued.

Connecting Mozambique to the world

The first MSC agency in Mozambique was founded in 1995. Since then, MSC Mozambique has expanded to cover the country’s three main ports of Maputo, Beira and Nacala. Today, we have more than 130 employees based in our offices in Maputo, Beira and Nacala, in addition to our depot and warehouse in Beira.

We offer global network coverage as well as local market knowledge. Our services further extend along the logistic corridors to the neighbouring countries of Malawi, Swaziland, Zimbabwe, Zambia, South Africa and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Through the work of our dedicated teams of experts and the support of our valued clients, MSC has become the leading container shipping line in the country and a dominant force on the inland transportation corridors that connect Mozambican ports to the region.

Container deposit

Import container release

All import container releases are subject to a container deposit as outlined in MSC Mozambique’s Local Charges Tariff Book.

This deposit is charged to limit the agency's liability over import containers. The container deposit will be fully refunded once the empty container is returned in good condition to the line’s stock and after all outstanding amounts related to the importer’s account are settled.

Link copied!

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard. This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing MOZ customs inspections, or while the cargo inside the container is being reworked for safety reasons.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the terminal, rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

For more details contact your MSC Agency.

Share
Link copied!

SOLAS VGM information for the Mozambique

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, all marine terminals in Mozambique are now allowed to use their certified scales to record shipment VGM.

What to include in VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking number

Vessel, ETA, POL

Container number

Seal number

Commodity

VGM and unit (e.g. 15Ton or 15,000kg)

Authorized person’s signature, shipper or nominated representative and stamp.

How to submit VGM instructions?

myMSC (free of charge)

Manually, fax, emails – subject to administrative fees as per Local Tariff

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo at Container Terminal

NO VGM – NO LOADING

Deadlines for sending VGM declaration

The shipper must submit the VGM declarations to MSC 48 hours before ETA of the vessel.

Prohibited cargo

It is illegal to bring the following items into to Mozambique.

Imports

Merchandise with fabrication labels of false commerce or origin, books and works of art when they are counterfeit editions

Objects, photographs, albums, recordings of sound or images and film of a pornographic nature or other materials that were judged offensive to public morals and dignity

Imitations of formulas of postal franchise used in the country

Medication and food products harmful to public health

Food products that are harmful to public health that cannot be used for other purposes

Distilled alcoholic drinks that contain essences or chemical products recognized as harmful such as: Aldeido Benzoico, Badia, Eteres silicitos, Hissopo e Tulinana

Hallucinatory and psychiatric substances except when imported for hospital use

Other merchandise whose prohibition of importation is established by special legislation

Certain gases as specified below:

Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)

Halogens (Halon 1211, Halon 1301 and Halon 2402)

Carbon Tetrachloride of Carbon (CCL4)

Other substances banned as per the Montreal Protocol as regards substances that destroy the ozone layer as ratified by Resolution No. 8/93 of the 8th December

Left-hand drive vehicles used for commercial purposes. ‘Commercial purposes’ has been defined as:

Sale or resale to third parties

use in transport which generates income

use in support of income

Notas e moedas com curso legal no País, além dos limites definidos pelo Banco de Moçambique;

Colecções e obras de arte que constituam património artístico ou cultural nacional, à excepção do previsto no artigo 47 do presente Decreto;

Outras mercadorias cuja exportação seja proibida por legislação especial.

The period of freetime starts as of the day of empty container release and ends the day of the commercial proforma date – ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) communicated during your booking – of selected vessel. If the loading vessel changes upon customer’s request, the application the application period begins when the empty equipment is picked-up and stops the day of loading on board vessel.
