SOLAS VGM information

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

Government approval status

The French government has published since May 28th 2016 a decree with tolerance 5% inaccuracy allowed on two methods.

What to include in your VGM instructions

The following items are mandatory and must be in all VGM instructions :

Booking number or B/L number

The container number

The VGM in kg

The name of the responsible person in capital

letters, as electronic equivalent of the signature

How to submit your VGM instructions

myMSC.com

EDI (via INTTRA, GT NEXUS, Cargo Smart and any other)

Shipping instructions signed

Fax, email

Deadlines for sending your VGM instructions

VGM must be known to the ship-agent, at least 24 hours before physical closing of the vessel.

The VGM cut-off date will be mentioned on the booking confirmation. If the VGM is received later, the container will not be planned / loaded on the vessel.

Admin Fees and costs

If the VGM has to be handled manually by the local agent, a local fee of 100€ per container will be applied. This also applies for VGM info added in the electronic booking.

If the VGM is not received before VGM closing time, container will be put on hold and all related costs like demurrage, storage, moves, plugging… will be for the account of the shipper.

If the VGM declaration is wrong after loading on board, a penalty will occured of 500€ per container, extracost and collateral expenses will be invoiced.

Documentation requirement for RWANDA

All cargo arriving to and departing from RWANDA Cluster must be covered by below listed mandatory documents. These documents provide the relevant agencies with all information.

Acceptance – Import
Weight: General weight limitation is 23 tons/20’DV (all included) and 35 tons/40’DV (All included)
There has no overweight tax; vessels are not allowed to load overweight containers.

Dangerous Goods & OOG

Hazardous Cargo: According to IMO classification, some dangerous cargo (like explosives) shall be discharged in priority. Dar Es Salaam and Mombasa Ports will contact the local importer for the organization of priority discharge and immediate delivery.

Documentation
Following mentions are mandatory on the B/L: ORIGINAL, FREIGHT TO BE PAID AT, FREIGHT COLLECT or PREPAID. Signature of the Person Responsible at Port of Loading + date of B/L or Sea Waybill emission.
Destination local charges

Only following charges are accepted as Import local charges in RWANDA:
BL fee, delivery orders fee, manifest correction fee, Reefer containers plugged onto reefer points, genset lift on/off fee, genset in transit, detention and demurrage charges and local delivery charges.

Fines:

In case any of the documentation is not in order upon arrival of the vessels at the Port of Discharge, the shipping line will be fined for non-compliance. Any fines, costs and consequences will be debited to the offices of origin immediately for recovery from the shippers. These costs can’t be recovered from importers.

Terminal

The Queen Elizabeth II Quay in Freetown is recognized as the main entry point/exit point of cargo vessels to Sierra Leone.

The Port of Freetown, also known for its natural harbour was established in 1964 by an Act of Parliament- The Ports Act (No. 56) of 1964 and created the Sierra Leone.

In recent years, the core functions of the Ports were privatized through Concession Agreement granted to Africa Global Logistics (Freetown Terminal Limited) to operate the container terminal and Necter Sierra Leone Bulk Terminal (NSBT) to operate bulk and break-bulk cargoes. Meanwhile, the Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority (SLPHA) Act No. 29 was enacted in May 2023 (which repealed and replaced the Ports Act of 1964) primarily conferring landlord and created the Sierra Leone Ports Authority.

The Port of Freetown prioritizes security and safety and has over the years taken measures to keep the Port safe and secured. Accordingly, the Port of Freetown received a PASS in 2029 as being ISPS compliant after a security audit was conducted by the United States Coast Guard on ISPS code.

MSC operates services to and from the Freetown Terminal at the Queen Elizabeth II. The port operates with seven (7) major berths 1-4 for break bulk and 5 & 6 for RORO and 7 for container vessels

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

SOLAS VGM information

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in the USA are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments. Download our USA VGM policy and terminal guidelines for more information.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

Verified Gross Mass (VGM)

In line with the SOLAS (Safety of Life at Sea) regulations introduced by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), all packed containers must have a Verified Gross Mass (VGM) declared before loading.
Key VGM Guidelines:
• No container will be loaded unless its VGM is declared by the shipper.
• VGM must be submitted via NAVIS during the pre-advice process.
• MSC will extract VGM data directly from NAVIS for vessel planning and terminal coordination.
• Failure to submit VGM will result in the terminal refusing to handle the container.

Accepted VGM Methods
Method 1: Weighing the Packed Container
• The entire sealed container is weighed using calibrated and certified equipment.
• Weighbridges must comply with regulatory standards (contact SANAS or NRCS for guidance).
Method 2: Calculated Weight of Contents
• All cargo items, packaging, pallets, and securing materials are weighed individually.
• The container’s tare weight (visible on its exterior) is added to the total.
• This method requires certification and approval by SAMSA.
Note: Estimations are no longer permitted under SOLAS. Only verified weights are accepted.

VGM Submission Deadline
VGM must be submitted before the container enters the port terminal. Timely submission is critical for:
• Stow planning
• Safe vessel loading
• Regulatory compliance

Driving Precision in Automotive Logistics with MSC South Africa

With over 35 years of experience as a direct production line supplier to one of South Africa’s leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), MSC South Africa delivers precision-driven solutions tailored to the automotive industry. From components to complete vehicles, our expert team ensures your cargo moves securely, on time and with full visibility every step of the way.

Tailor Made Approach

Fast and reliable transit times

Production Line Precision & Reliability

We align with OEM production schedules to ensure just-in-time delivery of critical automotive parts. Our dedicated team offers:

• 24/7 tracking and updates

• Real-time visibility across the supply chain

• Urgent, high-care handling for all cargo for manufacturers and suppliers
We treat every shipment with the same precision and urgency as our OEM partners.

Strategic Port & Inland Connectivity

With strong operations in Durban, Cape Town, Port Elizabeth and East London, MSC connects South Africa’s automotive hubs to global markets. Our integrated inland network combines:

• Road and rail transport

• Efficient plant-to-port movement

• Reduced delays and optimized transit times

This ensures a smooth and reliable logistics flow from production to export.

Expert Vehicle Containerization

At MSC-owned facilities near major ports, we specialise in secure vehicle packing with expert containerisation for a wide range of vehicles. By reducing handling, we minimise the risk of damage, while sealed containers ensure security until the final destination. This process guarantees safe and efficient delivery, ensuring vehicles arrive ready for showroom display or fleet deployment.

Scalable Export Solutions for Growing Markets

As South Africa’s automotive exports continue to expand into Africa, Europe and Asia, MSC supports this growth with frequent sailings on key automotive trade routes, flexible scheduling aligned to production cycles, and scalable solutions for both small and large volumes. With end-to-end support covering everything from packing to documentation, we enable automotive brands to grow confidently across borders.

Did You Know?

South Africa exports over 300,000 vehicles annually, reaching more than 150 international markets. MSC South Africa plays a key role in this global reach by offering containerized vehicle solutions that reduce handling risks and ensure safe, secure delivery.

Africa

South Africa

Cold Storage

Durban’s Premier Cold Chain Hub

Welcome to MEDLOG Cold Storage, a cutting-edge 15,000m² facility in Durban designed to meet the growing demand for reliable cold chain logistics across South Africa and beyond. With capacity for 10,000 pallets of chilled and frozen goods, we offer a seamless, secure solution for importers, exporters and logistics providers handling temperature-sensitive cargo.

Strategic Location for Speed and Efficiency

Located just 8 km from the Port of Durban (Durban Harbour), and close to major empty container depots and the N3 highway, the state-of-the-art cold store is ideally positioned to support both import and export operations.

Advanced Cold Chain Technology

The Cold Store is equipped with CO₂ refrigeration systems, offering energy-efficient and eco-friendly cooling, precise temperature control across all zones, and mobile racking systems that minimize product handling and maintain product integrity. From citrus and dairy to frozen foods, we ensure optimal conditions for every commodity.

Fully Accredited & Compliant

MSC meets the highest international and local standards to
support your cold chain needs. The facility has BRCGS Food Safety
Certification, a first for Durban cold stores. As well as Occupational Health
& Safety Accreditation. It is registered with South Africa’s Perishable
Products Export Control Board (PPECB), Department of Agriculture, Land Reform
and Rural Development (DALRRD), Border Management Authority (BMA), and South
African customs. With bonded warehouse status and a capacity for 4,000 bonded
pallets, the facility enables deferred duty payments and secure export storage,
ensuring compliance and reliability at every step.

Integrated Landside Logistics & Digital Visibility

Durban Cold Storage offers a complete landside logistics solution,
featuring cold storage and handling, transport coordination, seamless warehouse
management system (WMS) integration with customers and third-party vendors, and
a customer portal for real-time access to stock, invoices, and documents. With
these services, you can enjoy full visibility, stock integrity, and
tailor-made, user-friendly solutions that simplify your operations.

Did You Know ?

Cold Storage plays a vital role in the citrus export supply chain, offering secure, accredited cold storage for fruit from South Africa, Botswana, and Eswatini. Our facility ensures quality preservation and efficient “onto ship” solutions, supporting exporters every step of the way.

Africa

Fruit

Connect South Africa’s Finest Fruit to the World

South Africa is a global leader in premium fruit exports - from citrus and grapes to avocados, apples and stone fruits. As international demand continues to grow across Europe, Asia and the Middle East, MSC South Africa plays a critical role in connecting local growers to global markets through specialized reefer logistics, strategic port access and door-to-door cold chain solutions.

Cutting-edge cooling technology

Dedicated reefer experts

Cold Storage warehousing solutions

Advanced Reefer Technology for Peak Freshness

Our state-of-the-art reefer containers, equipped with MSC iReefer smart monitoring, provide real-time visibility of temperature, humidity and cargo location. This ensures optimal control to preserve taste, texture and shelf life, delivering peace of mind from origin to destination.

Learn More

Strategic Port Access and Inland Connectivity

With a strong presence in Durban, Cape Town, Port Elizabeth, Coega and East London, MSC provides fast, reliable access to global trade routes and seamless inland movement from farm to port. Supported by our cold storage solutions and integrated landside logistics, our network ensures efficient, time-sensitive handling of fresh produce across the supply chain.

Compliance and Cold Chain Expertise

MSC South Africa works closely with PPECB, DALRRD and other regulatory bodies to ensure full compliance with export standards. Our reefer specialists oversee pre-trip inspections, Cold Treatment, Controlled Atmosphere protocols and container readiness for sensitive fruit cargo. This guarantees your fruit meets the highest quality and safety standards every time.

Scalable, Seasonal Door-to Door Logistics Solutions

From orchard to overseas, MSC South Africa offers:

• Door-to-door delivery

• Flexible scheduling to match seasonal volumes

• Dedicated reefer trade and sales teams providing real-time updates and market insights

Our personalized support helps you navigate peak seasons with confidence and agility.

Did you know?

South Africa is the largest citrus exporter in the Southern Hemisphere - and MSC is proud to be a trusted partner in delivering this world-class produce to global markets.

Africa

Intermodal

Intermodal Solutions beyond the Port

At MSC South Africa, we offer a fully integrated intermodal network that connects road, rail, warehousing, and mineral depot services - designed to move your cargo efficiently before and beyond the sea leg of its journey. With national coverage, a robust fleet, and expert teams, we provide tailor-made, end-to-end logistics solutions that take the strain off your inland shipping needs.

Road

Rail

Barge

Warehousing

One-Stop Shop for Inland Logistics

Our “one-stop shop” approach means less coordination, fewer delays, and more control—allowing you to focus on your core business while we handle the logistics. We simplify your supply chain by offering a comprehensive suite of services, including road and rail transport, warehousing and mineral depot services, container packing and unpacking, as well as specialized equipment and skilled staff.
Whether it’s general, bonded, hazardous, reefer, or out-of-gauge cargo, MSC delivers a single point of contact for all your inland logistics requirements.

National Footprint with Strategic Coverage

We provide seamless cargo movement across South Africa while ensuring efficient access to major ports and industrial hubs.

This strong local presence, combined with our national reach, allows us to deliver reliable support and expertise wherever our customers need it.

In addition, we cover key long-distance routes connecting Johannesburg with Durban, Cape Town with Johannesburg, and Port Elizabeth with Johannesburg.

Specialized Equipment & Fleet Strength

Our extensive fleet includes tipper trailers, side loaders, retractable trailers, lowbeds, and car carriers. In addition, we offer reefer containers and gensets, as well as flatbeds, sliders, hi-cube trailers, and super links. With dedicated fleets stationed in City Deep, Pretoria, Cape Town, Durban, Uitenhage, Coega, and East London, we’re equipped to handle in-bond cargo, hazardous materials, refrigerated and temperature-sensitive goods, as well as out-of-gauge cargo.

Overborder Capabilities Across Southern Africa

MSC supports cross-border logistics into key regional markets, including Lesotho (via Durban – truck only), Eswatini (rail & truck), Botswana (rail & truck – Gaborone, Francistown), Zimbabwe (truck – Harare, Bulawayo, Gweru, Mutare), Zambia (truck – Lusaka, Kitwe, Ndola), and Malawi (truck – Lilongwe, Blantyre).

Did You Know?

Our strongest value proposition is our one-stop shop approach combining infrastructure, equipment and expertise to deliver a seamless inland logistics experience. Whether you're moving containers, minerals, vehicles or temperature-sensitive cargo, MSC South Africa has the network and capability to get it done efficiently and reliably.

Africa

South Africa

Minerals

Your Trusted Partner for South Africa’s Mining Sector

For decades, MSC South Africa has been a trusted logistics and shipping partner for the mining and minerals extraction sectors, helping local producers reach global markets efficiently and reliably.
South Africa’s rich mineral resources are vital to industries such as construction, manufacturing, energy and technology. MSC’s extensive global network and dependable transit times ensure your supply chain remains resilient and responsive to market demands.

Global Coverage

Reliable transit Time

Door-to-door Solutions

We Handle Top Commodities

At MSC South Africa, we specialize in the transportation of
key mineral commodities, including Chrome, Manganese, and Lithium. While copper
is not handled directly, we offer reliable shipping solutions to move copper
cargo globally.

Expertise in Mining Logistics

MSC has deep industry knowledge from mine to market. With a strong presence in key mining regions, we understand the complexities of mineral cargo—from heavy bulk shipments to sensitive classifications—and ensure smooth, compliant transport every step of the way. Our teams provide seamless support from origin to destination—so you can focus on your core business with confidence.

With Strategic infrastructure in Johannesburg

Our dedicated Mineral Depot in Johannesburg serves as a strategic hub for handling, storing and dispatching mineral cargo. It’s part of our commitment to delivering efficient, secure and scalable logistics solutions for South Africa’s mining industry.

Johannesburg <-> Durban

Port Elizabeth <-> Johannesburg

Did you know?

South Africa isn’t just rich in scenic beauty—it’s also a global powerhouse when it comes to chrome and manganese. These two minerals are recognized as “high-critical” under the country’s new Critical Minerals and Metals Strategy, reflecting their growing importance in global supply chains.
Chrome is the secret behind stainless steel’s shine and durability, while manganese is not only vital for steel manufacturing but is increasingly important in lithium-ion battery cathodes, supporting the global shift to clean energy.

Project Cargo

Project Cargo Solutions for South Africa’s Logistics Landscape

From mining machinery to industrial components, MSC South Africa specializes in oversized and out-of-gauge shipments that require expert handling and tailored logistics. Our Project Cargo team delivers safe, secure, and cost-effective solutions designed for South Africa’s infrastructure, industries, and trade corridors.

Expertise in Oversized Cargo

Access to Ports
and Terminals

Out of gauge Handling

End-to-end Solutions

Local Expertise in Complex Cargo Handling

South Africa’s terrain and infrastructure transport systems
demand specialized advanced logistics expertise. MSC South Africa offers
customized solutions for heavy-lift project and breakbulk cargo, backed by
decades of experience. Our team provides feasibility studies and route
planning, as well as IMO-compliant lashing and securing plans. We ensure your
cargo is handled with precision, safety, and full regulatory compliance.

Strategic Access to South Africa’s Major Ports

With strong operational hubs in Durban, Cape Town, and Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), MSC connects you to South Africa’s key maritime gateways. Our close relationships with port authorities and service providers allow us to optimize transit times, reduce costs, and ensure smooth cargo handling. Whether you're exporting mining equipment or importing industrial goods, we streamline your cargo journey.

Breakbulk & Out of Gauge Cargo Solutions

We provide custom solutions for unconventional cargo.
Out-of-gauge cargo is securely lashed onto platforms, flat racks, or open-top
units using specialized techniques and equipment. We focus on loss and claim
prevention, ensuring smooth delivery of even the largest and heaviest cargo.

End-to-End South African Services

MSC South Africa also offers comprehensive support beyond
the port. Our inland collection and delivery are managed with specialized
purpose-built trailers and lifting equipment, ensuring your cargo is
transported safely and efficiently. Our
services include stevedoring, port lashing, and storage at all major ports,
offering complete peace of mind as your cargo transitions through key gateways.
For additional flexibility, we provide on-site cargo securing and depot-based
handling options.

Thermal Liner

Advanced Protection for South African Cargo

MSC Thermal Liner is a high-performance cargo protection system made from linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), blended with nylon and aluminium. This unique composition gives it a metallic finish, exceptional durability and superior thermal insulation, making it ideal for South Africa’s variable climate and demanding export conditions.
Installed as a liner bag inside shipping containers, MSC Thermal Liner safeguards cargo against temperature fluctuations, moisture damage and contamination risks—all common challenges in the logistics industry and cold chain management.

Door-to-door expert support

Wide range of equipment

Sensitive cargo protection

Climate-Resilient Thermal Shielding

With scorching summer heat and sudden winter cold snaps, South Africa’s changeable weather puts cargo at constant risk. MSC Thermal Liner’s reflective material helps stabilize internal container temperatures, drastically reducing damage caused by thermal shock and heat stress.

Moisture Control for Sensitive Goods

Before loading, calcium chloride moisture absorbers are placed inside the liner to actively reduce humidity. This is especially critical for moisture-sensitive commodities such as charcoal, coffee, cocoa, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals, ensuring product integrity from origin to destination.

Easy Installation with Expert Oversight

Installation begins with a container inspection to ensure structural integrity. The container is cleaned thoroughly, and the liner is fitted by trained professionals to guarantee optimal performance. This process ensures that the liner functions as a sealed barrier against external contaminants.

Next-Generation Thermal Protection Now in South Africa

The MSC Thermal Blanket is a cutting-edge cargo protection solution engineered for South Africa’s demanding logistics environment. Crafted from a high-performance blend of aluminium and polyethylene, it offers unmatched defense against temperature swings, moisture buildup, and harsh weather conditions.

Download  EPR PDF

Did You Know ?

Putting moisture absorbers in the MSC Thermal Liner keeps the cargo safe and dry. They capture both humidity and condensation, the main culprits behind moisture damage during transit.

Wine

Unlocking Global Opportunities for South African Wine with MSC

South Africa’s wine industry is globally celebrated for its quality, heritage, and growing international demand. With exports reaching over 130 international markets, including the United Kingdom, Europe, North America, and Asia, MSC South Africa plays an essential role in facilitating the international distribution of locally produced wines.

Through our specialized reefer solutions, expert cargo handling and strategic port access, MSC South Africa ensures every bottle is shipped with care, precision and freshness.

Specialized Equipment for Bulk Wine Exports

Around 60% of South Africa’s wine exports are shipped in bulk using flexitanks or 20’ containers. MSC’s Cape Town depot offers:

• Consistent availability of 20’ GP containers

• Technical expertise for flexitank preparation and packing

• Flexitank supply and fitting services

We simplify the process from vineyard to vessel, ensuring efficiency and product integrity.

Reliable Global Reach

With frequent sailings and dependable transit times, MSC connects South African wineries to key global destinations. Our expansive network ensures efficient delivery to over 130 countries with reliable scheduling to meet market demands, giving wineries the confidence to expand their international footprint.

Temperature-Controlled Shipping Solutions

Wine is highly sensitive to temperature fluctuations, which is why MSC South Africa provides refrigerated containers with optimal climate control and real-time monitoring. This ensures taste, aroma and shelf life are preserved, so every bottle arrives in perfect condition - ready for retail or tasting.

Integrated Inland and Port Connectivity

From the vineyards of the Western Cape to South Africa’s major ports, MSC’s integrated logistics network provides smooth inland transport and timely port access. With end-to-end solutions that minimise delays and support just-in-time delivery, we help wineries meet international demand with precision and reliability.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

SOLAS VGM information

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in the USA are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments. Download our USA VGM policy and terminal guidelines for more information.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s empty container released for stuffing.  No free time in case of empty containers released and subsequently returned to MSC upon booking cancellation.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable for the use of import containers after the free time expires.

Detention and demurrage: updated payment policy:

The following options are available for release of shipment from Detention and Demurrage hold.

· For immediate release, payment thru electronic transfers to the designated bank accounts of MSC Tanzania.

· Payment by cheque is acceptable. However, the shipment will be released ONLY once cleared and funds received.

In case of a demurrage or detention dispute, email: tz060-credit.control@msc.com; tz060-customerservice.team@msc.com  (email subject: Dispute + Invoice Number), describing the reasons for your dispute.

Questions about detention/demurrage charges?

SOLAS VGM information for Tanzania

VGM Receiving Policy in Tanzania /or/ SOLAS VGM: a new regulation for a safer supply chain /or/ SOLAS VGM information for Tanzania

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

· Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

· Container number

· VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

· Responsible Party Name

· Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

· MyMSC (Free of Charge)

· EDI (via INTTRA)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

· MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) at before cargo is submitted for Customs Declaration until or before cargo is to be transferred to the Port.

· TZ Ports have “NO VGM – No GATE” policy in place

Questions about VGM?

Contact our MSC Tanzania team.

Detention, demurrage, and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the full import container gate out from the terminal, or for the empty container delivered for export.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires for full import container discharged and still on the terminal.

A storage charge is applicable after the free time expires for the occupied space by the container in the terminal. It is invoiced by the terminal operator directly to the customer.

SOLAS VGM information for MSC Togo

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, all marine terminals in TOGO are now allowed to use their certified scales to record shipment VGM.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM and weight measurement unit (kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before planning containers on the vessel. This helps to be sure that VGM details are well submitted before loading containers.

The ultimate deadline for VGM submission is three days before vessel arrival.

Please note: Shipments without VGM submission will be postponed to the next available vessel and hold fees (USD 25 per TEU per day) will be applied.
Questions about VGM?

Contact: TG467-vgmtogo@msc.com

Container Tracking Number

A container tracking number (CTN) is mandatory for all cargo entering Togo or in Transit to hinterland countries.

What is CTN or BESC?

A CTN is an electronic cargo tracking note submission to ANTASER (the validation service for the value of goods), which must be made by the importer or forwarding agent before the cargo is discharged at Lomé port. CTN only applies to cargo arriving in or transiting through Togo.

The CTN must be completed before the arrival of the goods at the port of Lomé.

When the goods are in transit, two CTNs are requested: one each for Togo and for the country of destination.

The CTN is a document which indicates the parties to the contract and the characteristics of the goods (Shipper, Consignee, Notify, Carrier, Vessel name, POL, POD, BL number, Container numbers, incoterm, Description of goods, Hs code, Cargo weight, Packages, Sea freight, Insurance premium, others cost, Freight payment place etc...)

It must be completed before the goods are declared to customs. The customs service uses it to validate the value of the goods.

Please Note: Importers who do not submit the CTN upon vessel departure can submit it at destination before clearance of the goods at the customs. But the POL must ensure that below clause is inserted in the manifest: "The shipper has not been able to provide the ECTN /BESC reference at the time of shipment. in consideration of the shipper not complying with the ECTN /BESC regulation, he hereby agrees to indemnify MSC and MSC Togo S.A., their respective servants and agents and to hold all of them harmless in respect of any liability, claim, or expenses of whatever nature which any of them may sustain by reason of non-production of ECTN /BESC number in accordance with Togo import local requirements”

For more details, see: www.antaser.com

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention and demurrages?

Demurrage and detention are be calculated by a fixed charge times the number of days the container was held for after the free period of 12 days.

Detention and demurrages in import are the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for not returning an empty container to MSC container yard.

Detention in export is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for not entering the container in the Marine Terminal.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the Marine Terminal at Rades Port. Storage charges have to be settled to the Stevedoring Company STAM.

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified. VGM weight of containers is performed by the local stevedoring company STAM inside Marine Terminal.

VGM has to be communicated to MSC agency before loading. No container can be loaded without VGM.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

Connecting  Zimbabwe to the world

With offices in Harare and Bulawayo and an unrivalled global network, we help connect Zimbabwe’s businesses to the world. Whatever you need to ship, we have the local and global expertise needed to get it to its destination on time wherever in the world that happens to be. From our container depot in Harare’s industrial area, our road and rail network connects you via the ports of Beira in Mozambique and Durban in South Africa. From here, the rest of the world is just a short hop away. MSC Zimbabwe was established in 1981.

Fully digitalized, we connect to MSC's worldwide computer network so Zimbabwean exporters and importers can manage their shipments online. In 2001, we opened a dedicated empty container depot in Harare's Industrial Area. The MSC Container Depot facilitates the fast and smooth release of equipment to shippers and delivery of empty containers to customers in Zimbabwe. In addition to convenient road access for trucks, Zimbabwe also offers direct rail links to and from Beira and Durban.

Our strengths and features MSC is the only line in Zimbabwe to:

● Own and run a container depot

● Have self-owned offices

● Provide reliable landside delivery by rail and road

● Offer a full package of services from customs clearance, import and export road and rail carrier haulage, door collections and delivery

● Be linked globally through gateway ports to destinations across the globe

● Offer customs clearing services for both imports and exports

● Facilitate the release of containers in both Harare and Bulawayo. We look forward to providing you with second-to-none transportation solutions!

SOLAS VGM information for Zimbabwe

What is VGM?

Verified gross mass (or VGM) refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, all marine terminals are now allowed to use their certified scales to record shipment VGM in case of any doubt regarding customer submissions.

What to include in VGM instructions

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM and weight measurement unit (lbs or kgs)

Name of responsible party

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in CAPITAL LETTERS.

How to submit VGM instructions

myMSC  (free of charge)

Email: zwe-exports@msc.com

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) 24 HOURS before vessel arrival in port Beira or Durban. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against Zimbabwean cargo by both Ports of Loading, which will be billed to the Shipper of Record. This also helps to avoid cargo being declined at load port.

Currently all cargoes loading from both ports of loading servicing Zimbabwe abide by the SOLAS policy.

All rail shipments must have the VGM submitted within 24 hours of the container gating in at the origin rail ramp, to avoid any extra fees levied by the terminal for weighing services.

SOLAS VGM information for Guatemala

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in Guatemala are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible party name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of charge)

EDI (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Manually (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Email: GT495-COMMERCIAL@MSC.COM (note: the email will only be monitored for VGM declarations)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

We encourage customers to submit their Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo at Guatemala port of loading, which will be billed to the shipper of record.

Any shipper of record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal.

For truck delivery, the ultimate deadline for VGM submission will be 12:00 noon local time on the day of the cargo cut-off.

There are currently no Guatemala terminals with a “NO VGM – No GATE” policy.

All rail shipments must have the VGM submitted within 24 hours of the container gating in at the origin rail ramp to avoid any extra fees levied by the terminal for weighing services. Late gates will only be considered for approval when a VGM is submitted by the shipper of record before 12:00 noon, local time, on the day of the cargo cut-off.

MSC admin fees and costs

Manual VGM Submission Fee (applies to email, fax, and inclusion on standard shipping instructions): 25 USD per container.

Late VGM Submission Fee: 25 USD per container.

VGM Misdeclaration Fee: 300 USD per misdeclaration, per container.

Questions about VGM?

Contact our Guatemala Team: GT495-COMMERCIAL@MSC.COM

Detention, Demurrage, Per Diem and Storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the customer warehouse.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing customs inspections, or while the cargo inside the container is being reworked for safety reasons.

In case of a demurrage dispute, email: samantharaphaela.lafalaise@msc.com - (email subject: Dispute + Invoice Number), describing the reasons for your dispute.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, or container yard.

In case of Per Diem disputes, email: samantharaphaela.lafalaise@msc.com - mentioning the invoice number in the email subject. Please describe the reasons for your dispute.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the marine terminal or container yard (for the use of the land).

Detention and demurrage: updated payment policy

Please note our D & D agency collection (DECSA) will no longer accept check copies or written guarantees to release shipments from detention and demurrage hold.

The following options are available for release of shipment:

For immediate release, payment must be submitted directly to DECSA.

If the payment cannot be done directly to DECSA, payment by check is acceptable.

SOLAS VGM information for Haiti

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in Haiti are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments. Download our Haiti VGM policy and terminal guidelines for more information.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

EDI (via myMSC)

Manually (via myMSC)

Emails: rachelle.abdon@msc.com and yvrose.belinette@msc.com (note: the emails will only be monitored for VGM declarations)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

We encourage customers to submit their  Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo at Haiti port of loading, which will be billed to the shipper of record

Any shipper of record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal

For truck delivery, the ultimate deadline for VGM submission will be 48 hours of vessel ETA

MSC admin fees and costs

VGM misdeclaration fee: 150 USD per misdeclaration, per container

Late VGM submission fee: 25 USD per container

Terminal fee for VGM service is 50 USD

Questions about VGM?

Contact our Haiti team.

SOLAS VGM information for Honduras

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

After resolution issued by the Marina Mercante, which states that all containers must be certified by the scale provided directly by the port terminal (Operadora Portuaria Centro Americana OPC). The VGM transmission to the shipping line will be done directly at the terminal (OPC).

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

EDI (directly from the terminal to responsible parties)

Admin Fees and Costs

As from July 1st, 2016, all containers must be weighed at the terminal prior to being loaded.

Weigh tolerance +/- 3%

The shipper is fully responsible to pay all charges at the terminal regarding VGM processes. If these costs are not paid to the terminal prior to the vessel`s arrival, the container will not be loaded.

MSC Mexico connects the country to the world's major trade routes through a global network of shipping, logistics, and intermodal transportation solutions. With nearly three decades of experience, we have established ourselves as a strategic partner for importers and exporters, supporting the growth of international trade from one of Latin America's most dynamic markets.

As a regional benchmark within the organization, MSC Mexico also plays an important role in strengthening Central America's connectivity with major global markets, facilitating trade and creating new growth opportunities for our customers. Backed by a global network, a long-term vision, and a strong commitment to service excellence, MSC Mexico keeps the world moving by connecting businesses, markets, and people.

LOI (Letter of indemnity) for lost or destroyed OBLs (Original Bills of Lading)

What is an LOI?

An LOI (Letter of Indeminity) is required when an original Bill of Lading is lost or destroyed. It can be completed by shipper at the Port of Loading, or by the consignee at the Port of Discharge.

The LOI requires 200% of the commercial value of the cargo plus Ocean Freight to be guaranteed either through bank or MSC’s Insurance company.

MSC’s global LOI requirements are set out by our Geneva headquarters. The LOI must be completed as per these instructions in order for a duplicate Bill of Lading to be issued.

Detention, Demurrage and Storage charges in Nicaragua

What is Detention?

Detention is a charge applied when a container remains in the customer’s possession beyond the free time granted by the carrier. It covers the use of the carrier’s equipment outside the terminal, including time spent at the consignee’s or shipper’s facility. Detention charges may also apply while the container is undergoing customs inspections or when cargo must be reworked for safety or compliance reasons.

What is Demurrage?

Demurrage is a charge applied when a container remains within the marine terminal, railroad facility, or container yard beyond the allocated free time. These charges accrue until the container is removed from the terminal.

If you need to dispute a demurrage invoice, please contact ni623-disputas@msc.com with the subject line: Dispute + BL Number + Invoice Number, and include a detailed explanation of the reason for your claim.

What are Storage Charges?

Storage charges are assessed by the terminal or customs warehouse when containers remain at their facilities beyond the free storage period granted.

Detention and Demurrage – Payment Policy

• For immediate cargo release, payment must be made via wire transfer or ACH.

Questions About Detention and/or Demurrage Charges?

SOLAS VGM information for Nicaragua

VGM Receiving Policy in Nicaragua/or/ SOLAS VGM: a new regulation for a safer supply chain /or/ SOLAS VGM information for Nicaragua

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Company name

Address

Location

Postal code

Country

Weighing Date

Container number

Responsible party name Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of charge)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

We encourage customers to submit their Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered at port (from Monday to Wednesday prior to vessel arrival). This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo at the port of loading, which will be billed to the shipper of record.

Any shipper of record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal.

MSC admin fees and costs

Manual VGM Submission Fee: 25 USD per container.

Late VGM Submission Fee: 25 USD per container.

VGM Misdeclaration Fee: 25 USD per misdeclaration, per container.

Questions about VGM?

Contact: nic-cs.export@msc.com

Prohibited Cargo

It is illegal to bring the following items into or out of Nicaragua:

Radioactive material and explosive.

Used cars that have exceeded ten years since their manufacturing date.

Household goods must be consigned to a freight forwarder (FFW must provide legal representation certificate for customs clearance). In case of diplomatic cargo consigned to a FFW, copy of diplomatic ID and record of migration movement must be submitted to the customs authorities.

Specific restrictions for Democratic People's Republic of Korea (Customs reference CT/076/2019):

Food & agricultural products - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes included in Chapter 12)

Soil and stones (including magnesite and magnesia) - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes included in Chapter 25)

Timber - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes included in Chapter 44)

Iron, steel, and metals - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes from Chapter 72 to 83)

Machinery - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes included in Chapter 84)

Electric equipment - (Central America Tarif System/SAC: HS Codes included in Chapter 85).

Media with immoral or seditious content, such as child pornography.

Drugs, narcotics, and some medication containing prohibited substances.

Items infringing trade and copyright regulations.

Container Weighing (VGM)

All MSC local offices provide certified scales to record and verify container weight (verified gross mass or VGM) in line with Safety of Lives at Sea (SOLAS) regulations. VGM instructions are mandatory for all shipments for safety reasons and vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been appropriately verified. Detention, Demurrage and Storage charges in Panama

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable in exports, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container by the shipper. This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing customs inspections, or while the cargo inside the container waiting for departure vessel (based on proforma date), these are calendar days and include holidays.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable in imports, after the free time expires, inside or outside the terminal, these are calendar days and include holidays.

In case of a demurrage dispute, email PA595-collections@msc.com (email subject: Dispute + Invoice Number), describing the reasons for your dispute.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the terminal and handled by PSA Rodman. This charge is invoiced directly by MSC.

Paying detention and demurrage charges

All payments must be done directly to our bank account via` wire transfer or certified check. Once completed, please make sure to upload payment confirmation to our online platform: 2vision.mscpanamacounter.com

DEMURRAGE

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

Eight (8) free calendar days will be granted for dry cargo (or those negotiated), and three (3) free calendar days for refrigerated containers.

The free days are continuous, including Saturdays, Sundays and holidays without exceptions. They are counted from the day after the discharge date.

Demurrage: Updated Payment Policy

The Collection Department will no accept check copies or written guarantees to release shipments from demurrage hold.

The following options are available for the shipment release:

For immediate release, payment must be submitted via wire transfer to our local bank accounts detailed at the bottom of the invoice.

If payment cannot be done by wire transfer, payment by cheque or ACH is acceptable. However, the shipment release will be effective ONLY after funds are confirmed with the local bank.

To find out your demurrage pending balance, please contact the Collection Department py746-cobranzas@msc.com.

Unblock Containers

To unblock the container at the terminal after paying the demurrage, please contact the Customer Service team PY746-customerservice@msc.com or the Commercial team PY746-commercialpy@msc.com.

EXCHANGE OF IMPORT DOCUMENTS

To make the exchange of import documents, you must present the following documents at our offices:

Exchange Code sent by the agency, after payment of the pending invoices.

Original letter of guarantee signed by the consignee + stamp (legal person).

1 original BL endorsed by the consignee and notify + stamp (legal person).

Invoices of local charges and freight must be cancelled, if the payment chosen is COLLECT (payable at destination).

If the type of release is EXPRESS, you must present the BL + a note in English endorsed by the consignee + stamp (legal person).

FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions)

Do you handle the import of used tires?

Yes, we handle the import of used tires. The only condition is that freight is payable at origin and is accompanied by a cargo approval (acceptance of the cargo).

Do you handle importation the import of used vehicles?

Yes, we handle the import of vehicles manufactured up to 10 years before their clearance at the customs office at origin. If older, the importer must present the amparo appeal in order for the booking to be confirmed.

Do you operate in the ANNP Villeta terminal?

MSC does not operate at the ANNP Villeta Terminal. In case you need the container to be transferred to this terminal, you must request the inclusion of the following clause in the BL: “cargoes in transit to VILLETA ANNP under merchant’s risk and account”. This will allow the receiver/consignee to manage the transfer by truck from the private port offered by MSC to VILLETA ANNP. MSC will not be responsible for the transfer.

What charges applies with the INR (Retention Tax)?

In accordance with the provisions of Law 6830/19, Art. 75 and 76, a 4.71% retention tax will be applied to freight, accessories, and delays for collect shipments.

Export

DETENTION

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container inside and outside the terminal. This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing customs inspections, or while the cargo inside the container is being reworked for safety reasons.

The export detention in Paraguay is divided into two periods: first, outside the terminal, and then inside it.

Detention outside the terminal - Ten (10) days: This period is counted from the date of pick-up of the empty container until the return of the full container to the terminal.

Detention inside the terminal - Seven (7) days: This period is counted from the entry of the full container into the terminal until its loading date.

Once the days have expired, the tariff will be applied:

Detention: Updated Payment Policy

The Collection Department will no longer accept check copies or written guarantees.

The following options are available for the detention payment:

Payment must be submitted via wire transfer to our local bank accounts detailed at the bottom of the invoice.

If payment cannot be done by wire transfer, payment by check or ACH is acceptable.

To find out your detention pending balance, please contact the Collection department py746-cobranzas@msc.com.

LATE BL RELEASE (LBR)

It is a penalty for the non-payment of the set of cash invoices that enable the release of the maritime BL in any of its printing types (Telex/Express Release and Print at POD).

To avoid this extra cost, payment must be made within the first 15 days from the date of issuance of the invoices. After 15 days, the costs apply.

FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions)

What are the requirements to ship metal scrap cargo?

It is mandatory to present the following documents:

Transit authorization note in the territory of the Argentina Republic issued by the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development of Argentina (transshipment requirement).

Certificate issued by the Secretary of the Environment of Paraguay.

Both documents/certificates must be valid at the time of proceeding with the shipment.

What are the requirements to ship charcoal cargo?

It is mandatory to present the self-heating certificate, with a sample collection date no greater than 5 days before the date of the shipment. Only certificates from the AQUAGROUP Laboratory are accepted.

Charcoal shipments are NOT accepted in BULK.

Pro-liner bags: These are thermal bags that protect cargo from high temperatures and lower the level of oxygen to reduce the risk of combustion on board. The bags also protect the cargo from any increase in humidity due to variations in climatic factors during the trip. The use of these bags is mandatory for charcoal cargo.

Vanning survey through the MSCI+ application: This is an MSC application to facilitate the customer’s inspection of charcoal/briquette shipments. Keeping a record of the charcoal shipment inspections on this application is mandatory. For the user request and guidance on the MSCI+ app, contact our Customer Service team PY746-customerservice@msc.com.

What are the weight limitations for shipments?

It is the responsibility of the exporter/booking client to verify weight limitations in destinations that involves land, river and/or train (Inland/On-carriage) transportation.

Is fumigated cargo considered IMO (dangerous cargo)?

Fumigated cargo inside the container is considered IMO (dangerous cargo). It must be specified at the time of requesting the quote. The procedure and rate will be different from a non-dangerous cargo.

LWS (Low Water Surcharge)

The LWS is an emergency charge applied to guarantee the safety in the navigation, the crew, and the cargo during the low water rivers season.

This charge is applied for both import and export cargo, depending on the resolution issued by the General Naval Prefecture of Paraguay at the time of the barge nomination.

Demurrage for Peru Imports

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable after the free time expires, for the usage of a container in import status.

In Peru, demurrage is collected in advanced, which means that before the empty unit returned, all demurrage charges should be collected and invoiced.

In case of demurrage disputes, please send an email to MSC Peru Demurrage Control Team PER-demurrage.detention@msc.com, showing the details of the dispute, the BL number and other additional information regarding your case in the email´s subject.

Payment flow of demurrage

Whenever a Demurrage payment is performed, this should be addressed to MSC Peru Invoicing Dept PER-invoicing@msc.com, including the general information of the shipment for invoicing purposes.

Questions about demurrage and other solutions linked to these costs?

In case you need assistance regarding the following topics, you can contact us or use our online solutions.

1. To validate the demurrage free days granted for an import shipment, you can go to our website EXTRANET MSC PERU using the BL number and the option “Calcular Sobreestadía”: See Here.

2. To validate the demurrage charges generated by an import shipment, you can go to our website EXTRANET MSC PERU using the BL number and the option “Consultar Sobreestadía”: See Here.

3. To obtain the “Memorándum de Devolución”; which is a document that establishes the place, condition, and time for returning the import units, you can go to our website EXTRANET MSC PERU using the BL number and the option “Descargar Memo”: See Here.

BLs to order – Shipments to USA- CANADA

The USA & Canada Customs regulations allow to manifest endorsed BLs complying with the following requirements:

The consignee must read “TO ORDER OF (ANY COMPANY)”.  It is not allowed the expression “TO ORDER” neither in Spanish (A la orden de..)

The following terms can be used:

To order of

To order of Shipper

To order of the Shipper

To the order of

To the order of shipper

In case of:

To Order of Company: Consignee complete details must be included.

To Order of a Bank: All the bank details, including contact and address, must be declared.

The Notify must always be the real receiver with an address in the USA.

For cargo “in transit” through USA & Canada, the same requirements apply, but the Notify should not be necessarily in the USA or Canada. And a second Notify could be manifested.

SOLAS VGM in Peru

Government approval status

The authority in charge of implementing this procedure in Peru is the National Port Authority (APN).

The tolerance between the VGM submitted by the client versus the weight registered at the marine terminal should not exceed 3%.

Controls can be random

All scales for the VGM providers must be duly certified by INACAL (National Institute of Quality).

Containers can enter the marine terminal without a VGM, but they will not be loaded until the VGM is submitted to the shipping line

What to include in your VGM instructions?

Booking number

Container number

VGM + unit (Kgs)

Authorized person’s signature (submitter of the VGM who may be authorized to act on behalf of shippers)

Responsible party name

How to submit your VGM instructions?

myMSC

EDI (via Terminals - INTTRA)

Deadlines for sending your VGM instructions

24 hours before vessel´s ETA.

Admin fees and costs

MSC will apply an administrative fee in the following cases:

VGM is submitted late, after the aforementioned deadline.

Misdeclaration fee when MSC finds a discrepancy between the VGM submitted by the shipper versus the weight reported by the port terminal.

Recommendations

All units must enter the marine terminal with a valid VGM certificate. In case the same is missing or the discrepancy is higher than the authorized tolerance (3%), the shipper must request the terminal to issue a new VGM, otherwise, the container will not be loaded, and all related costs will have to be faced by the shipper.

Special Customs Regulations

Special Customs Regulations

As of November 14, 2016, the Peruvian Customs requires Tax ID number of consignee and Notify to be specified in the manifest. The Tax ID number is called RUC in Peru.

TAX ID will be declared through the MSC code. Tax ID manifested to Peruvian Customs will be based on MSC Code, manifesting agents have to ensure that the TMS code used from cnee/notify should include TAX ID info.

Please include this mandatory information in the Shipping Instructions for all your shipments to Peru. Customs will apply a fine or other measures if the manifest does not include this information.

For further information, please contact: PER-import.documentation@msc.com

For donation cargo, shipment must be previously accepted by our Imports Department, together with the LOI signed by the shipper, taking responsibility for any uncovered charges at destination.

Consider for the transit and transhipment cargo at the port of Callao – our local authorities request that description must be shown in detail with the quantity of packages of the cargo. Otherwise, cargo is going to be seized as they are “undeclared cargo” for Peruvian Customs.

Consider that import cargo with error data or incomplete in fields of consignee or description, will be subject to a fine of US$ 140.00 per BL.

Through Supreme Decree No. 005-2020-MTC and in accordance with Article 1 of Legislative Decree No. 843 that regulates the minimum quality requirements for the import of used vehicles, the following was modified:

Article 1.- Since November 1, 1996, the importation of used motor vehicles, for the transport of passengers or goods, that complies with the minimum quality requirements indicated below, was modified as follows:

a. Be no older than two (2) years. The age of vehicles is calculated from the model year. The import of used vehicles with compression ignition engines (diesel) of categories L, M and N, except for subcategories M3 and N3, is prohibited.

Other considerations about Peruvian Customs Regulations:

Used spare parts for vehicles (cars) and used tires are prohibited/restricted products.

Important note: The importation of used motors, parts and pieces destined for land transport are only allowed for certain HS codes and must be remanufactured and have the documentation required (Authorization from the supplier of remanufacture, certificate of the remanufacture, warranty certificate of the fabric specifying that auto parts have been remanufactured) For more information, please consider the following links: INFORME N° 012-2021-SUNAT/340000; Decreto Supremo N° 058-2003-MTC (Art, 144 and 148).

Machinery for the industry is allowed, such as truck, forklift, etc - vehicles that are not operated within the National Road Transportation System.

As per Peruvian regulation, the maximum time allowed to clear cargoes in all Peruvian ports should not exceed 15 calendar days (legal abandonment).

After this period, cargoes are kept under Customs Authorities control.

Consignees can still recover their cargoes, but they have to deal directly with Customs Authorities through a Customs Agent and pay all fines (provided the cargo was not already sold in a public auction).

Blueberries

A Leading Force in Global Blueberry Exports

Peru has become the world’s leading exporter of fresh blueberries, driven by sustained growth and continuous investment in production and logistics. Blueberries are now one of the fastest-growing commodities within the country’s agro-export sector.

Production is concentrated in northern regions such as La Libertad and Lambayeque, where proximity to ports and efficient logistics are critical to maintaining fruit quality. As a highly perishable product, blueberries require precise temperature management and consistent cold chain performance.

MSC supports Peruvian blueberry exports with tailored reefer solutions, combining local expertise, reliable operations and global connectivity.

Strong Reefer Capacity

Cold Chain Control

Outstanding port coverage

Packing and value-added facility in Piura

Reliable Capacity for Growing Blueberry Industry

Blueberry exports require consistent access to equipment and efficient logistics planning throughout the entire season. MSC supports exporters with strong equipment availability and the operational scale needed to support increasing export volumes with consistency.

With a global network and ongoing investment in infrastructure, MSC is well-positioned to support the continued growth of Peru’s blueberry industry. Combined with direct access from Callao, Pisco and Paita, exporters benefit from efficient cargo flow and reliable export execution for high-value shipments.

Cold Chain Control and Compliance for Blueberry Exports

Maintaining cold chain performance is essential to preserve blueberry quality across all export destinations. We combine proven Cold Treatment expertise with consistent service performance to support seamless execution and reduce operational risks.

Through Food Safety Management (FSM) protocols and MSC iReefer, exporters benefit from temperature stability, real-time visibility and proactive monitoring throughout the journey.

Explore Reefer Solutions

Additional Protection for
High-Value Shipments

Blueberries are a high-value commodity where temperature deviations can impact product quality and commercial outcomes. MSC Extended Protection (EPR) provides an additional layer of coverage against risks such as temperature variation due to refrigeration interruption.

With simplified claims handling managed by MSC specialists, exporters gain additional security and peace of mind.

Explore Protection for Your Reefer Cargo

Integrated Logistics Close to Production Areas

Efficient first-mile logistics are essential to preserving blueberry quality. MSC supports exporters with operations close to production areas in northern Peru, including packing capabilities in Mórrope and Piura, combined with inland transportation and container availability.

Access to strategically located depots in Paita, Callao and Pisco enables efficient container pick-up and positioning, reducing unnecessary transport, streamlining operations and improving cargo flow from origin.

Did you know?

Peru is the world’s leading exporter of fresh blueberries, supplying key markets such as the United States and Europe with steady volumes throughout the year.

Real-Time Reefer Monitoring for Blueberry Exports

Track and monitor your reefer containers throughout the journey with MSC iReefer, ensuring full visibility and control of your cargo conditions.

LEARN MORE

Plan Your Blueberry Shipments with MSC Peru

Connect with our local experts to optimize your blueberry exports with reliable, end-to-end logistics solutions.

Supporting Peru’s Citrus
Export Industry

Peru is a growing counter-season supplier of citrus, exporting mandarins, Tahiti limes, oranges and tangelos to global markets. Production is concentrated in the coastal valleys of Lima, Ica and northern Peru, supported by a strong agro-export sector.

Exporters must meet strict phytosanitary standards and Cold Treatment protocols while maintaining fruit quality throughout the entire supply chain. MSC supports citrus shipments with year-round services from Paita, Callao and Pisco, including uninterrupted operations in southern Peru.

Advanced Reefer Visibility

Cold Treatment Transit Planning

Outstanding port coverage

Packing and value-added facility in Piura

Connected Shipping for Peru’s Citrus Exports

Peru’s citrus exports depend on consistent shipping connections and precise logistics coordination. MSC links the country’s main citrus producing regions with global markets such as Northern Europe and the U.S. East and West Coast, helping exporters move regulated citrus cargo with confidence.

Our transit times to key gateways such as Philadelphia are aligned with Cold Treatment timeframes, allowing the protocol to be completed seamlessly during the voyage.

Additional Protection for Fresh Citrus Cargo

MSC Extended Protection (EPR) provides additional protection for reefer cargo, covering risks such as damage, theft and prolonged refrigeration interruption. With simplified claims handling and dedicated MSC specialists, exporters gain additional security for their shipments and commercial commitments.

Explore Protection for Your Reefer Cargo

Enhanced Cargo Monitoring with FSM

Maintaining stable temperature conditions is essential for citrus shipments. MSC’s Food Safety Management (FSM) protocols provide enhanced supervision of reefer cargo through the MSC Control Tower, monitoring temperature stability and compliance with cold chain requirements.

Combined with MSC iReefer visibility through myMSC, exporters can monitor container conditions throughout the journey.

Explore Reefer Solutions

Did you know?

Demand for Peruvian mandarins and Tahiti limes continues to grow across North America and Europe thanks to their counter-season availability.

throughout the journey.

Mango

Shipping Mangoes
with Confidence

Peru is one of the world’s leading producers of Kent mangoes, exporting mainly to Europe, the US and Asia. With most export volumes originating in the northern regions, particularly Piura, exporters rely on efficient reefer logistics, real-time visibility and access to packing and cold-chain services to preserve freshness and meet international demand.

MSC Peru supports the entire mango supply chain with reliable equipment availability, operational expertise, and logistics solutions located near the main orchards and packing facilities.

Reefer container (40’ High Cube) availability

Controlled atmosphere

Dehumidification systems for optimal fruit preservation

Packing and value-added facility in Piura

"
Trust is the key behind every fresh mango that reaches its destination. With MSC iReefer, you get real-time visibility, precise temperature control, and peace of mind knowing your fruit is protected throughout the entire journey.
"

Erika Arias
Reefer Manager

Weekly Global Connections from Paita

During the Peruvian mango season, exporters depend on predictable departures to protect product quality and access key markets. MSC Peru supports your planning with weekly sailings from Paita, complemented by additional calls at Callao and Pisco to maintain cargo flow when volumes peak.

With strong coverage across the country and consistent transit options, we help you align shipments with harvest windows and reach international destinations with stability.

End-to-End Cold Chain
for Peruvian Mangoes

Located in Piura, our packing and processing facility is strategically positioned near the main mango-producing valleys — Tambogrande, San Lorenzo and Alto Piura in Piura, as well as Olmos and Motupe in Lambayeque.

This proximity shortens inland transit, speeds up post-harvest handling and strengthens cold-chain protection during the harvest peak.

A Team That Understands
Your Season

Our reefer specialists and on-ground operations teams understand the sensitivities of exporting Peruvian mangoes, including temperature control, harvest timing and inland handling.

They coordinate documentation, reefer pre-inspection, inland transport and export planning to protect product quality and maintain cargo flow throughout the season.

Did you know?

More than 95% of Peru’s fresh mango exports come from the northern valleys of Piura, Lambayeque and Ancash.

Real-Time

Monitoring

for Mangoes

Track temperature, humidity and ventilation in real time with MSC iReefer to protect quality throughout your export journey.

Explore our iReefer Solution

Talk to our local reefer experts

Get tailored guidance for your mango exports, from packing to shipment.

Detention, demurrage, Per Diem and storage charges

What is detention?

Detention is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s full container inside the marine terminal, railroad facilities or container yard. This charge can also apply while the container is undergoing US customs inspections, or while the cargo inside the container is being reworked for safety reasons.

What is demurrage?

Demurrage is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, inside the terminal for the use of the land.

In case of a demurrage dispute, email US038-nydetention@msc.com (email subject: Dispute + Invoice Number), describing the reasons for your dispute.

What is Per Diem?

Per Diem is the charge applicable, after the free time expires, for the use of the carrier’s container (full or empty) outside the marine terminal, rail ramp or container yard.

In case of Per Diem disputes, email US038-PerdiemDisputes@msc.com, mentioning the invoice number in the email subject. Please describe the reasons for your dispute in accordance with terms of the UIIA: https://www.uiia.org

Our dispute team will come back to you within 48 business hours.

What are storage charges?

A storage charge is applicable, after the free time expires, for containers left inside the rail ramp or container yard (for the use of the land).

Paying detention and demurrage charges through E-Pay

To pay by credit card, log onto https://e-pay.mymsc.com/iPayment/ and enter your invoice number (not BL or CNTR number). You can then add it to the cart and proceed with the payment. Both you and our Demurrage/Detention group (team?) will receive the payment confirmation. We will then proceed with the release and will notify you accordingly. So, in this case, you do not need to email

US038-nydetention@msc.com.

Detention and demurrage: updated payment policy

Please note that DDP Department will no longer accept check copies or written guarantees to release shipments from Detention and Demurrage hold.

The following options are available for release of shipment:

· For immediate release, payment must be submitted via credit card.

· If the payment cannot be done by credit card, payment by cheque or ACH is acceptable. However, the shipment will be released ONLY after funds clear.

SOLAS VGM information for the USA

What is VGM?

Verified Gross Mass or VGM refers to the exact, verified weight of a packed container. For safety reasons, vessel operators can only load a container if its weight has been verified.

In line with SOLAS (Safety of Lives at Sea) regulations, all marine terminals in the USA are now allowed to use their certified scales to record Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of shipments. Download our USA VGM policy and terminal guidelines for more information.

What do I need to include in my VGM instructions?

You must include the following on all VGM instructions:

Booking or Bill of Lading (BL) number

Container number

VGM + weight measurement unit (lbs. or kgs.)

Responsible Party Name

Digital signature of the authorized signatory in all CAPITAL LETTERS.

How can I submit my VGM instructions?

myMSC (Free of Charge)

EDI (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Manually (via INTTRA; GT NEXUS; Cargo Smart)

Email: us038-vgmusa@msc.com (note: the email will only be monitored for VGM declarations)

Guidelines for submitting your VGM instructions

MSC prefers to receive a Shipper-Verified Gross Mass (VGM) before cargo is delivered. This helps to avoid any unexpected weighing charges being levied against the cargo at the US Port of Loading, which will be billed to the Shipper of Record.

Any Shipper of Record-signed VGM will override any VGM derived at or by the terminal.

For truck delivery, the ultimate deadline for VGM submission will be 12:00 noon local time on the day of the cargo cut-off.

There are currently no US terminals with a “NO VGM – No GATE” policy.

All rail shipments must have the VGM submitted within 24 hours of the container gating in at the origin rail ramp, to avoid any extra fees levied by the terminal for weighing services. Late gates will only be considered for approval when a VGM is submitted by the Shipper of Record before 12:00 noon, local time, on the day of the cargo cut-off.

MSC admin fees and costs

Manual VGM Submission Fee (applies to email, fax, and inclusion on standard shipping instructions): 25 USD per container.

Late VGM Submission Fee: 25 USD per container.

VGM Misdeclaration Fee: 300 USD per misdeclaration, per container.

LOI (Letter of indemnity) for lost or destroyed OBLs (Original Bills of Lading)

What is an LOI?

An LOI (Letter of Indeminity) is required when an original Bill of Lading is lost or destroyed. It can be completed by shipper at the Port of Loading, or by the consignee at the Port of Discharge.

The LOI requires 200% of the commercial value of the cargo plus Ocean Freight to be guaranteed either through bank or MSC’s Insurance company.

MSC’s global LOI requirements are set out by our Geneva headquarters. The LOI must be completed as per these instructions in order for a duplicate Bill of Lading to be issued.
